## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level

**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a
second approval by an owner of the same stack, which keeps it to two people (OD8). Confirmed by the owner
(OD13): the original author opens the approval PR and the first approver
approves it. If the first approver is unavailable, another owner of the stack approves; that makes
three people and is recorded as a deviation, counted monthly (OD11). A cross-team PR needs one
approval, as GitHub accepts one on-call group member for files of several owner teams (OD10,
OD9, 📖 R3.2.7); domain review there is a recommendation, counted in the monthly report. A real-data read is not a change and has its own rule, L3-data. Incidents use the same
path with faster people, not fewer security checks.

| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue and the rest of the canonical list in layer 5; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher. L3 paths (workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, the SCP stack): the L3 owner team only (OD13); IAM-only stacks are deployable, so the L3 owner team plus the on-call group (OD9). L3 content inside a domain file (an IAM statement in `serverless.yml`, a stateful delete): the stack's owner, then the risk stop (OD8). In incidents: the on-call approver for deployable paths (OD9); paths that define the process (CODEOWNERS, agent config, catalogue, workflows) wait for the L3 owner team | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b); incidents only, as the owner accepted it (Options §9 Q2); the on-call approver counts as owner of the service in the request (OD13) | layer 7 |
| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9; at night, see layer 6 | layer 6 |

`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
the whole team (OD3). With code-owner review on, every PR, L2 included, needs an approval from an
owner of the files it touches (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7; per-file behaviour ⚠️ not a separate research row).
What differs at L3 is **which team** owns the path: L3 paths are owned in CODEOWNERS by a designated
L3 owner team (deployable L3 paths also by the on-call group, OD9), L2 paths by their domain team; and IaC changes at L3 meet the
risk stop. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files, so they are approved by
the stack's owners, not the L3 team (OD8); automated checks make up for this: IAM Access Analyzer
`check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and the Pulumi policy pack (📖 R4.2.2), both from phase 2 (layer 5). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need the L3 owner team, not
the domain team that edits it most.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
- **L3 approvals [design]:** CODEOWNERS plus code-owner review only, no path-based required
  reviewers rule. That rule (📖 R3.2.4) asks for approvals from specific teams, which the on-call
  group would not satisfy at night, and how it combines several teams is not researched (⚠️), so it
  would break OD9 or add a third person. GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5), set by a dedicated GitHub App that reacts to review events and is the pinned source [design; hosting, key storage and whether its key counts against S2 are not researched, ⚠️ G19], adds what
  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3). A workflow
  instead of an app is weaker: pinning the source to GitHub Actions likely lets any workflow set a
  check of the same name, and the trigger that runs on review events from trusted code is not
  researched (⚠️ G19).
- **Who approves at night (OD9):** a fixed GitHub team with write permission (owners without it
  are silently not assigned, 📖 R3.2.7; the CODEOWNERS validation check covers this), the on-call approvers, is listed as
  co-owner on every deployable path in CODEOWNERS (infrastructure and service code), next to the
  domain team. Confirmed by the owner (OD13): the group does **not** co-own the paths that
  define the process (`.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md` and agent config, catalogue); those stay
  with the L3 owner team only. If a broken workflow blocks a night fix, the pipeline counts as
  unavailable and the JIT fallback applies (layer 7). One primary and one backup from that team are on call. Technically any member can approve any
  path; by rule the primary approves and the backup only if the primary is unavailable (OD2).
  Membership is fixed, not changed per shift [design]. GitHub team membership is set in organization
  settings, not by a PR; managing it as code (e.g. with Pulumi's GitHub provider) and the audit
  event for a membership change are not researched (⚠️ G16). Meanwhile the layer-7 settings
  comparison includes the group's member list. Cost: an approval from any
  listed owner satisfies code-owner review (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days a member could approve
  another domain's PR, on or off shift. Mitigation [design]: process rule "approve another
  domain's PR only if it carries the `incident` label and you are on shift", and a monthly report of
  every cross-domain approval by group members on PRs without that label (layer 7). Whether Papaya's team size allows full coverage is unknown
  (§1, S7).
- **Risk stop [design]:** applies to every deploy, whatever the level. The deploy job previews prod;
  on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change, a network or security-group change, or an advisory
  policy finding (from phase 2) it stops and posts the filtered preview. The original author opens a second PR that adds
  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` (`<sha>` = the stopped commit) holding that SHA and the
  preview hash; the workflow does not open it, because the setting that lets Actions create and approve PRs stays
  off (📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3). CODEOWNERS on `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` names the owners of that stack and the
  on-call group (OD8, OD9). The approver is ≠ author and may be the first PR's approver, who now sees
  the prod diff. Merging it triggers the deploy on the new HEAD, which previews again and continues
  only if the hash matches the approved one; if another PR merged in between, the hash differs and
  the deploy stops again (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). Cost: while a stack is
  stopped, later merges to that stack stop too until a matching approval lands; in an incident, a
  risky change already waiting on `main` blocks the fix for the same stack until it is approved or
  reverted. A
  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1). The risk
  stop is described for Pulumi and Serverless only; for k0s manifests (RBAC changes are the IAM
  equivalent) a `kubectl diff`-based stop is a candidate, not researched (⚠️ G1). Firebase deploys
  have no preview step in this design (⚠️ G2).
- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
  slow unrelated tests skipped [design]. A required check skipped by a path filter may stay
  pending and block the merge (open, Options §8); this directly affects S7.

**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)

The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
unavailable).

1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
3. R, a co-owner of `serverless.yml` through the on-call group (OD9), reviews the diff. If R
   catches a missing queue change, R does not fix it (OD7): E pushes the fix, the stale approval is
   dismissed, and R approves again, one more review round (Options §6). E merges.
4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.

**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.

**Cost / value.** One approver for every prod change, from the owners of the path; two approvals,
usually by the same approver, when the risk stop fires (OD13; OD11). Cross-team PRs: one approval (OD10). None in non-prod.
Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

## Layer 4 — Supply chain for MCP servers and plugins

**Principle.** Local MCP servers, plugins and hooks run with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5); remote MCP servers receive tokens and data.
Only reviewed, pinned entries from a catalogue are allowed. The catalogue is the inventory (P4c).
Review takes ≤ 5 working days (S6), or people work around it.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Plugins:** a private marketplace repo with `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (📖 R1.4.1), sources
  pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only). Managed `strictKnownMarketplaces` = Papaya only,
  `blockedMarketplaces`, `enabledPlugins: false` to pull one (📖 R1.4.2), checked before download and
  at session start (📖 R1.4.3). `disableSideloadFlags` rejects `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url`,
  `--agents`, `--mcp-config` but not `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add` (📖 R1.4.2). With
  `allowManagedHooksOnly`, plugin hooks run only for force-enabled plugins (📖 R1.5.4). User mods are
  blocked by the `allowManagedModsOnly` option under `pluginConfigs` → `cc-plugin-sec-default@builtin`
  → `options` (📖 R1.5.6). The version floor covers the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).
- **MCP:** "approved catalogue" = `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true`; without
  the lock users can widen it (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4). Match by `serverUrl` or `serverCommand`, never
  `serverName` ("not a security control", 📖 R1.3.3); `serverCommand` matches the exact argv (📖 R1.3.3), so the catalogue entry pins an exact package version in it [design].
  `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` (📖 R1.3.7). With MDM, `managed-mcp.json` gives exclusive control;
  it cannot come from server-managed settings (📖 R1.3.2).
- **Review checklist** [design]: publisher; local `stdio` or remote (📖 R6.4.3); what it reads and where
  it sends data, with a supplier-register entry and BAA/DPA status (⚠️ R5.6); no token passthrough
  (📖 R6.4.2); write tools for Slack, Linear, GitHub only where needed (⚠️ R6.5 #6); how the server authenticates (Linear and Slack: G9); pinned version,
  reviewer, date.
- **Known gaps:** no per-group targeting in server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.6, R1.4.4); tool
  description changes after approval are not covered (⚠️ research 6.6).

**Audit evidence.** Catalogue file in git (each entry = an approved PR); supplier register; OTel
`claude_code.plugin_installed` / `plugin_loaded` (📖 R1.4.6). MCP tool logging needs
`OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1` (📖 R1.3.8); it stays off until we know whether it logs tool inputs (⚠️).

**Cost / value.** Up to 5 days' wait for a new tool. Compliance gets an asset inventory and supplier
records.

## Layer 5 — CI/CD hardening

**Principle.** CI is the default production writer, so it is the main target. Short-lived,
least-privilege credentials per job. Every CI dependency is pinned. Agent-written code passes the same
checks as human code (S10).

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Credentials:** OIDC instead of keys and tokens in repository secrets, which any writer can read
  (📖 R3.4.1, R3.5.3b). Org default for `GITHUB_TOKEN` set to "restricted", `permissions:` per job (📖 R3.5.3).
  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase
  deploys may need a stored credential in GitHub: a kubeconfig or token for k0s, a Firebase token or
  service-account key for Firebase Hosting. The owner accepts this as an exception to S2 = 0 until it
  is checked whether k0s and Firebase deploys can use OIDC (OD1, OD6). Conditions [design]:
  - stored only as an **environment secret of `production`**, never as a repository secret. Anyone
    with write access can read repository secrets (📖 R3.5.3b), which would turn the exception into
    standing prod write for every engineer and their agent. Environment secrets and a deployment
    branch rule limited to `main` are available on Team for private repos (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3), and
    only the reviewed deploy workflow references the environment (layer 3);
  - the deploy job runs on GitHub-hosted runners. On self-hosted runners, jobs "are not run in an
    isolated container, even if they use environments", so environment secrets there must be
    treated like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5). Self-hosted runners "can be persistently
    compromised by untrusted code" from anyone who can open a PR, and runner groups limit only which
    repositories use them (📖 R3.5.2); in a monorepo any workflow can likely target the runner's label (⚠️ G15).
    How to restrict a runner to one workflow is not researched (⚠️ G15); just-in-time runners exist
    (📖 R3.5.2, not read in detail). If reaching k0s needs a self-hosted runner, that
    runner is dedicated to the `production` deploy, and the residual risk is recorded;
  - that environment secret is the single source of truth: no copy elsewhere (OD1);
  - an owner, an expiry and rotation in the exception register;
  - optionally a separate environment (e.g. `production-k0s`), limited to `main` and referenced
    only by the k0s/Firebase deploy workflow, so AWS deploy jobs cannot read these secrets
    [design].

  Residual risk: admins can change the environment, and a deleted environment comes back without
  protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); the alerts and settings comparison in layer 7 cover this. The exception
  covers **CI deploy credentials only**. Runtime credentials, such as a k0s autoscaler's AWS access to
  add or remove nodes, live in the cluster, not in GitHub; they follow layer 1 (no static keys, a
  role attached to the machine; ⚠️ not researched for k0s, G1).
- **Side paths:** Pulumi ESC, Pulumi Deployments and Serverless Dashboard providers reach AWS
  (📖 R4.4.9) outside the GitHub gate (⚠️ R4.4.9); not used for prod (⚠️ R4.6 #6).
- **Pinning:** workflow lockfile (`gh actions-lock`) or full SHA, enforced by the org policy "Require
  actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA" (availability on Team ⚠️); the lockfile does not pin reusable workflows, so
  the deploy workflow lives in the same repo (📖 R3.5.5; conclusion [design]).
- **CODEOWNERS** on `.github/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`,
  `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, `.devcontainer/` (📖 R3.2.8; list ⚠️ R6.5 #5, R6.3.11), plus
  `.npmrc` (registry redirection) [design], the policy packs, the SCP code and the
  catalogue file. This is the canonical L3 path list that layer 3 refers to. Not on it:
  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/`, owned by the stack's owners and the on-call group (OD8, OD9). The private plugin
  marketplace is a separate repo and needs its own ruleset and CODEOWNERS [design]. CI validates the file, because
  invalid lines are skipped silently (📖 R3.2.7).
- **No privileged triggers with untrusted code** (`pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` + checkout,
  📖 R3.5.4).
- **Agent review:** an independent agent (not the one that made the change) may post an automated
  review as an extra check; it never counts as an approval (GĐ-11).
- **Agents in CI:** `claude-code-action` with a custom GitHub App limited to Contents, Issues, Pull
  requests (📖 R1.7.8), whose own credentials are listed in the S2 inventory (⚠️ G19); Anthropic workload identity federation, not a personal OAuth token (📖 R1.7.6);
  `--restricted` and explicit `--tools` (D3; passing it through `claude_args` unverified, ⚠️ research
  6.9.4 Q5); a managed-settings file on the runner, which also guards against mods (📖 R1.5.6; for
  federation auth ⚠️); MCP set fixed by CI because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
  (📖 R1.3.5); never `environment: production` (⚠️ R3.6 #4). Hosted runners give `sudo` (📖 R3.5.1),
  so with `Bash` in `--tools` the runner file is advisory (⚠️ R3.5.1, R3.6 #4).
- **App-opened PRs:** a required check set by a dedicated GitHub App, pinned as its source (layer 3), confirms at least one approval by a
  human who did not trigger the run; counting approvals is not enough, since the app's own approval
  might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3; 📖 R3.2.5).
- **Required checks (S10):** from phase 1, secret scanning, dependency check, SAST (products: G4);
  from phase 2, IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and Pulumi policy packs
  (📖 R4.2.2). For Serverless stacks, Access Analyzer would check the IAM policies in the
  CloudFormation template that `serverless package` produces, against the deployed ones (⚠️ not
  researched); policy packs do not apply to them. Until phase 2, the only compensation for OD8 is
  the risk stop, which fires on every IAM change in the prod preview.

**Audit evidence.** Workflows and lockfile in git; audit-log events such as
`org.update_actions_secret`, `repo.set_workflow_permission_can_approve_pr`, `repository_ruleset.update`
(📖 R3.3.3, R3.5.6). An audit event for environment-secret changes was not researched (⚠️); the
settings comparison in layer 7 covers the S2 exception meanwhile. Check results per PR; secrets inventory (S2).

**Cost / value.** One-time migration to OIDC and pinned actions; slower action updates. Compliance
gets S2 and the same guardrails for agent and human code.

---

## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence

**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).

## Layer 7 — Observability, audit, incident response and break-glass

**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.

**On Papaya's stack**

- **Audit stores:**
  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (cost 📖 R2.6.3; selection
    ⚠️ R2.9 #5), which makes the archive
    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
    with an expected copy (G8);
  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
    lost-record events (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️), stream treated as PHI (⚠️ R2.7.3);
  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2).
- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
- **Drift [design]:** its own role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2). On a DIY S3
  backend, preview needs state-write permission (📖 R4.3.3); whether a refresh preview writes more
  than locks is open (⚠️ R4.6 #2, G14). So either the drift role gets state write (and the same
  trust care as the deploy role), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection is used (📖 R4.3.2, Pro+). The
  latter runs on Pulumi Deployments, which holds credentials to prod, so it re-opens a side path that
  layer 5 excludes and needs the same trust narrowing and audit (📖 R4.4.9; ⚠️ R4.6 #6). CloudFormation
  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers the named approver schedule (primary + backup engineers, 24/7), as
  decided in framing round 1, and, because of OD7, a minimal incident-responder schedule; the
  latter extends that decision. The primary approves; the backup steps in only if the primary is
  unavailable (OD2). On-call approvers only approve during their shift; the fix is written by an
  incident responder (OD7). Alert routing and the
  rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5); in phase 1 the responder calls the approver by phone from the published schedule.
- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:

  | Step | Rule |
  |---|---|
  | When | Only during an incident (Options §9 Q2), when the PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. Outside incidents, an operation not in IaC waits for IaC or a runbook. |
  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant (Options §4b; OD7; backup rule OD2). |
  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`; role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3), so the real window can approach 2 h; ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which must keep the user blocked for at least 12 h (📖 R2.4.4). Applying it is a management-accou
  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |

  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."

  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
  this draft). On a breach,
  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
  (D2, ⚠️).

**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail; exported GitHub audit log; change records and monthly
reconciliation (S3, S8 ≤ 30 min); JIT requests, reconciliations, codify PRs; drift tickets; on-call
schedule and approval waits (S7); monthly report of cross-domain approvals by on-call group members
on PRs without the `incident` label (OD9).

**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
incidents, plus detection.

---
---

# 05 — Kế hoạch deliverable (chốt sẽ nộp gì)

## English summary

- **Purpose:** fix exactly what is submitted before the final writing pass. No new design decisions here;
  this note only decides form, order, length and scope.
- **Docs (§1):** a one-page `README.md`, then numbered docs: framework (trimmed from ~11k to ~8k words),
  a new short engineer guide, rollout plan 30/60/90 (moved out of framework layer 8), a compliance
  "control and evidence register" (not only a standards mapping), the existing threat model and
  problem→control map, the 10 existing ADRs, and three Mermaid diagrams.
- **Writing order (§2):** change workflow (layer 3) and identity & access (layer 1) first, each written
  together with its examples, because every other file refers to them; supporting docs after; README last.
- **Examples (§3):** 7 core and 3 secondary artifacts, each tied to a framework claim and to a local check.
  Main pushback on the initial idea: "environment approval" does not exist for private repos on GitHub
  Team (research R3.1.2), so the gate example is a **ruleset on `main`**, not environment reviewers; an IAM
  permission set alone proves little, so the OIDC trust policy and an SCP are added; the risk stop, the
  least proven part of the design, gets a runnable classifier with fixtures; "CrossGuard" is now called
  Pulumi Policies and is a phase-2, secondary item.
- **Excluded (§4):** anything that would need invented facts (k0s, Firebase, GCP configs), running tools
  against real targets, implementations of open gaps (JIT tooling, required-check app), and new decisions.
- **Open questions for the owner (§5):** framework length, the engineer guide, renaming docs with number
  prefixes, the scope of tier B, installing missing linters.

> Working note. Updated: 2026-11-09 · Status: draft, chờ owner chốt §5
>
> Ký hiệu: ✅ kiểm trong session này · 📖 R*x.y* = dòng trong `work/02-research.md` · ⚠️ chưa kiểm.

---

## 0. Hiện trạng (đầu vào của plan)

| Đã có | Kích thước ✅ (`wc -w`) | Trạng thái |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/framework.md` | 11 026 từ, 779 dòng | Owner duyệt (mục 1), 17 vòng review |
| `docs/adr/0001…0010` + `README.md` | 450–600 từ mỗi ADR | Owner duyệt (mục 2), 4 vòng review |
| `docs/threat-model.md` | 3 039 từ, 20 threat | Owner duyệt (mục 3), 3 vòng review |
| `docs/problem-control-map.md` | 3 194 từ, 40 dòng | Commit sau mục 4 |
| `README.md` | khung, ghi "skeleton only" | Phải viết lại |
| `examples/`, `diagrams/` | trống (`.gitkeep`) | Chưa làm |

Nhận xét dẫn tới plan này:

1. **Framework quá dài cho người đọc đầu tiên.** 11k từ ≈ 45–50 phút đọc. Panel lãnh đạo sẽ chỉ đọc §1.
   Layer 8 có một ô bảng (phase 1) dài khoảng 450 từ, khó đọc như một kế hoạch.
2. **Compliance chưa có một tài liệu của riêng mình.** Evidence nằm rải ở đoạn "Audit evidence" của 8 layer;
   bảng ISO/HIPAA ở layer 8 chỉ có 4 dòng, mã ISO là nhớ lại chưa đọc (⚠️ R5.1).
3. **Engineering chưa có câu trả lời ngắn cho "ngày làm việc của tôi thay đổi thế nào".** Có, nhưng rải ở
   layer 2 (session types), layer 3 (ví dụ 2 giờ sáng), layer 4, 6, 7.
4. **Framework hứa "copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`"** (`docs/framework.md:11`) nhưng `examples/`
   trống. Đây là chỗ hở lớn nhất so với quyết định hình thức deliverable (framing Q14).

---

## 1. Danh sách file sẽ nộp

Người đọc: **LĐ** = lãnh đạo / panel quyết định · **CO** = Compliance · **KS** = kỹ sư (engineer, DevSecOps).
Độ dài là mục tiêu, không phải giới hạn cứng. Thứ tự theo tiền tố số là thứ tự đọc (quy ước `CLAUDE.md`).

Ghi chú về các lựa chọn khác với gợi ý ban đầu:

  việc nào không chờ ai, việc nào chờ ai và bao lâu. Đây là mục có thể cắt nếu thiếu thời gian (§5 Q2).
- **Rollout tách ra file riêng**, và layer 8 chỉ giữ principle + link. Lý do: tránh hai bản rollout lệch nhau.
- **Ba sơ đồ**: chọn ba thứ khó diễn đạt bằng chữ nhất (luồng có nhánh, ranh giới tin cậy, trình tự theo thời
  gian). Không vẽ sơ đồ rollout (một bảng là đủ).
- **Nguồn sơ đồ ở `diagrams/*.mmd`, render `.svg` bằng `mmdc`** (✅ có sẵn, 11.12.0), nhúng `.svg` trong docs.
  Một nguồn duy nhất; render thành công là bước kiểm.

---

## 2. Thứ tự viết và lý do

| Bước | Việc | Vì sao ở vị trí này |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Đóng băng quyết định: OD1–OD13, D1–D3, Options §9. Lập danh sách thuật ngữ (L0–L3, risk stop, on-call approver, incident responder…) dùng thống nhất | Bản cuối là biên tập, không phải thiết kế lại. Mọi thay đổi quyết định phải quay về owner |
| 1 | **Lõi A — Change workflow (layer 3)** + examples E1 ruleset, E2 CODEOWNERS, E3 workflows, E7 risk stop | Là câu trả lời trực tiếp cho câu của Compliance ("named person approved"). ADR 0001, 0003, 0004, 0010, threat model và rollout (điều kiện cứng) đều tham chiếu nó. Viết example **cùng lúc** với văn bản để ép văn bản chính xác: nếu ruleset JSON không biểu diễn được điều văn bản nói thì văn bản sai |
| 2 | **Lõi B — Identity & access (layer 1)** + E4 OIDC trust, E5 SCP, E6 permission set | Là câu trả lời cho câu của Engineering ("talk to AWS directly"): agent được gì, không được gì. Viết sau layer 3 vì layer 1 dựa vào "ghi prod chỉ qua pipeline role" mà layer 3 định nghĩa; E4 phụ thuộc tên environment và workflow ở E3 |
| 3 | Layer 2 (agent runtime), 4 (supply chain), 5 (CI hardening) + E8 managed settings, E9 marketplace, E10 policy pack | Là lớp hỗ trợ / hygiene (ADR-0007). Phụ thuộc lõi nhưng lõi không phụ thuộc chúng |
| 4 | Layer 6, 7, 8; tách `03-rollout-plan.md`; viết `04-compliance-mapping.md` | Rollout cần danh sách control cuối và điều kiện cứng từ bước 1–2. Register cần đoạn "Audit evidence" cuối của mọi layer |
| 5 | Ba sơ đồ | Vẽ khi văn bản đã ổn định, nếu không phải vẽ lại. Mỗi sơ đồ được đối chiếu ngược với văn bản (sơ đồ không được nói điều văn bản không nói) |
| 6 | Đồng bộ phần phụ thuộc: threat model, problem-control map, ADR README (link, số layer, mã G/OD) | Bằng grep có hệ thống, không đọc lại bằng mắt |
| 7 | Engineer guide, rồi README | Cả hai là bản tóm tắt; viết cuối để tóm đúng bản cuối |
| 8 | Review độc lập toàn bộ (Rule 4) → sửa → review lại đến khi hết HIGH/MEDIUM; quét secret/PII; kiểm link; chạy `examples/validate.sh`; copy transcript | Cổng chất lượng trước khi nộp |

Mỗi bước 1–4 có review độc lập riêng trên phần vừa viết, theo Rule 4 trong `CLAUDE.md`.

---

## 3. Config mẫu trong `examples/`

Nguyên tắc chọn: mỗi file phải (1) chứng minh một claim cụ thể trong framework hoặc một ADR, và (2) kiểm được
**cục bộ**, không chạm hạ tầng thật (Rule 4). File không qua được cả hai thì không đưa vào.

Mọi file dùng placeholder (`<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>`, `123456789012`, `<org>/<repo>`), có comment đầu file trỏ về
layer/ADR, và marker cho trường/khóa chưa kiểm. Một script `examples/validate.sh` chạy toàn bộ kiểm tra;
output thật được dán vào `examples/README.md` (✅).

### 3.1 Tier A — lõi (phải có)

| # | File | Chứng minh điều gì | Kiểm bằng |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | `examples/github/ruleset-main.json` | ADR-0003: merge vào `main` là cổng duyệt. 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale, approval ≠ last pusher, required check có source app được pin, cấm force push, bypass list rỗng (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5) | `jq` (cú pháp) + JSON Schema của request body "create repository ruleset" lấy từ GitHub REST OpenAPI description (⚠️ chưa thử trích schema). Thêm test Python: các rule bắt buộc có mặt, `bypass_actors` rỗng |
| E2 | `examples/github/CODEOWNERS` | Layer 3/5: danh sách L3 path chuẩn chỉ thuộc L3 owner team; on-call group đồng sở hữu path deploy được nhưng **không** đồng sở hữu path định nghĩa quy trình (OD9, OD13); `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` thuộc owner stack + on-call (OD8) | Script `examples/tests/check_codeowners.py`: (a) mọi path trong danh sách L3 chuẩn ở layer 5 có mặt; (b) on-call team không xuất hiện trên path quy trình; (c) mỗi dòng đúng dạng `pattern owner…`. GitHub có endpoint báo lỗi CODEOWNERS (📖 R3.2.7) nhưng cần repo thật → không dùng |
| E3 | `examples/github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml`, `pr-preview-nonprod.yml` | Điều kiện "merge approval = deploy approval" (layer 3): chỉ workflow deploy tham chiếu `production`; không input ref/SHA; không `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run`/`issue_comment`; concurrency theo stack, không `cancel-in-progress`; `permissions:` theo job; OIDC (`id-token: write`); action pin SHA; PR chỉ preview non-prod. **Environment `production` chỉ có branch restriction + secrets, không có required reviewers** (xem ghi chú dưới) | `actionlint` + `zizmor` (linter bảo mật cho Actions) — cả hai **chưa cài** ✅ (`command -v`), cần cài (§5 Q5); `yamllint` ✅ có sẵn |
| E4 | `examples/aws/oidc-trust-prod-deploy.json` | Layer 1/ADR-0008: role deploy prod chỉ tin `sub` = `repo:<org>/<repo>:environment:production`, `aud` = `sts.amazonaws.com` (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4) | `jq` + test Python: điều kiện `sub` là `StringEquals`, không wildcard. Access Analyzer `validate-policy` là API AWS → không dùng (Rule 4). Linter offline (ví dụ `parliament`) ⚠️ chưa kiểm còn bảo trì và có hỗ trợ trust policy |
| E5 | `examples/aws/scp-prod-ou.json` | Layer 1: deny `lambda:UpdateFunction*` trừ deploy roles và JIT roles; revocation Deny theo `identitystore:UserId`; bảo vệ org trail; deny data-plane read trên claim store trừ role ứng dụng / data-read (danh sách action chưa đủ, ⚠️ G13) | `jq` + test: kích thước ≤ 10 240 ký tự (📖 R2.3.2); chỉ có `Deny`. Ghi rõ không chạy được policy simulator (cần AWS) |
| E6 | `examples/aws/permission-set-prod-read-metadata.json` | Layer 1/ADR-0002: `ProdReadMetadata` chỉ đọc metadata, session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4); không có action data-plane | Test Python: không có action nào trong danh sách data-plane đã biết (`s3:GetObject`, `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue`, …), không có `*` |
| E7 | `examples/risk-stop/classify_preview.py` + `fixtures/*.json` + `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` + `test_classify.py` | Phần mới và ít được chứng minh nhất của thiết kế (risk stop, [design]): từ output preview, phát hiện replace/delete stateful, thay đổi IAM, network/security group → dừng; tính hash preview để so khi deploy lại (Options §1) | `pytest` trên fixtures. Hạn chế ⚠️: fixtures viết tay theo dạng JSON của `pulumi preview --json` trong docs, không sinh từ Pulumi thật (Pulumi chưa cài ✅, và Rule 4). Fixture Serverless từ `serverless diff --json` cũng viết tay (📖 R4.4.2) |

### 3.2 Tier B — hỗ trợ (nên có)

| # | File | Chứng minh điều gì | Kiểm bằng |
|---|---|---|---|
| E8 | `examples/claude/managed-settings.phase1.json`, `managed-settings.phase2.json` | Layer 2/ADR-0007 và phân pha OD4: phase 1 chỉ các khóa ở layer 8; phase 2 đủ baseline (sandbox, `allowManagedHooksOnly`, `allowedProviders`…) | JSON Schema `https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json` qua Python `jsonschema` (✅ có sẵn). ✅ đã kiểm 2026-11-09: schema có 12/14 khóa cần dùng, **thiếu `allowedProviders` và `managedSourcesBehavior`** → kết quả kiểm phải ghi rõ hai khóa này chỉ có nguồn 📖 docs |
| E9 | `examples/claude/marketplace/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` + `catalogue-entry.example.md` | Layer 4/ADR-0006: catalogue là marketplace nội bộ, nguồn pin theo `sha`; mẫu bản ghi review một MCP/plugin (checklist layer 4) | `claude plugin validate <path>` — ✅ subcommand có trong Claude Code 2.1.319 (`claude plugin --help`). Chạy cục bộ, không cài plugin |
| E10 | `examples/pulumi-policy/` (TypeScript, 1–3 policy) | Layer 5 / OD8: thứ bù cho việc owner stack duyệt thay đổi IAM — ví dụ mandatory: cấm IAM `Action: "*"`, Aurora phải có deletion protection, S3 claim bucket phải chặn public | `npm ci && npx tsc --noEmit` (cần cài package, không chạm cloud). Không chạy được trên stack thật ⚠️. Tên sản phẩm hiện là **Pulumi Policies**; "CrossGuard" là tên cũ (📖 R4.2.1) |

### 3.3 Tier C — chỉ làm nếu còn thời gian

- `examples/github/workflows/claude-ci-agent.yml` (claude-code-action với GitHub App riêng, `--restricted`, `--tools`):
  nhiều điểm ⚠️ (truyền flag qua `claude_args`, PR do app mở được tính tác giả thế nào — R3.7, G19).
  Nếu làm thì gắn nhãn "illustrative" rõ ràng.

### 3.4 Phản biện gợi ý ban đầu (phần examples)

| Gợi ý | Đánh giá | Thay bằng / bổ sung |
|---|---|---|
| "GitHub Actions OIDC + environment approval" | **Sai với thiết kế đã chốt.** Trên GitHub Team, repo private không có required reviewers cho environment (📖 R3.1.2; giả định gói Team đã owner chốt, framing GĐ-5). Một example dùng `required_reviewers` sẽ mâu thuẫn ADR-0003 và làm người chấm nghĩ thiết kế dựa vào tính năng không có | E3 dùng environment chỉ cho branch restriction + environment secrets; cổng duyệt là **E1 ruleset**. Có thể thêm một comment "nếu lên Enterprise thì thêm required reviewers" |
| "IAM permission set" | Đúng nhưng chưa đủ: một permission set chỉ chứng minh quyền đọc. Ranh giới thật ở layer 1 là trust policy của role deploy và SCP | Giữ E6, thêm E4 và E5 |
| "CODEOWNERS" | Đồng ý; là nửa còn lại của cổng | E2 kèm script kiểm, vì GitHub bỏ qua dòng sai mà không báo (📖 R3.2.7) |
| "managed settings" | Đồng ý, nhưng là hygiene (ADR-0007), không phải lõi | Tier B, tách hai file theo phase để thể hiện OD4 |
| "Pulumi CrossGuard policy" | Hữu ích nhưng là control phase 2, chỉ bù cho OD8 | Tier B (E10), dùng tên Pulumi Policies |
| Thiếu | Ruleset `main` — artifact quan trọng nhất (chính là "named person approved") | E1 |
| Thiếu | Risk stop — điểm [design] mới nhất, chưa có gì chứng minh nó làm được | E7 |
| Thiếu | Catalogue plugin/MCP — ưu tiên số 3 trong 30 ngày (framing Q8) | E9 |
| checkov (nêu trong yêu cầu như ví dụ công cụ) | Không dùng làm công cụ chính: checkov quét Terraform/CloudFormation/Kubernetes/Actions; file IAM ở đây là JSON thuần, và hỗ trợ của checkov cho JSON IAM rời ⚠️ chưa kiểm. Có thể chạy checkov trên workflow (E3) như kiểm thêm nếu cài được | `actionlint` + `zizmor` cho workflow; test Python cho policy |

---

## 4. Cố ý KHÔNG đưa vào

| Không đưa vào | Lý do |
|---|---|
| Đề xuất thay Pulumi/Serverless/GitHub Actions; ví dụ Terraform | Ràng buộc cứng của đề (`CLAUDE.md`) |
| Config cụ thể cho k0s, Firebase, GCP | Chưa research (G1–G3). Viết ra là bịa; framework chỉ nêu nguyên tắc ở mức này (framing Q7) |
| Chương trình Pulumi đầy đủ cho Identity Center / SCP stack | Không chạy được (không có Pulumi, Rule 4); JSON policy đã đủ chứng minh nội dung |
| Code JIT (TEAM sample, bot Slack), code GitHub App cho required check | Là gap mở (G19, G20) hoặc lựa chọn sản phẩm chưa làm; một bản code minh họa sẽ trông như đã thiết kế xong |
| Runbook SSM Automation | Phase 2, chưa kiểm (OD4, G6) |
| Cấu hình paging/alert routing | Phase 2, công cụ chưa chọn (G5) |
| `managed-mcp.json`, cấu hình MDM | Không biết Papaya có MDM (layer 2) |
| Bảo mật AI agent production | Ngoài phạm vi (framing §1.4, A7a) |
| Statement of Applicability đầy đủ, phân tích pháp lý HIPAA/luật VN | Ngoài chuyên môn; HIPAA có áp dụng hay không là câu hỏi pháp lý (⚠️ R1.11.1.11). Register chỉ trỏ tới mã điều khoản với marker |
| Ước tính effort / chi phí bằng con số | Không có dữ liệu; framework đã ghi "effort not estimated" |
| Slide, deck, trang web | Hình thức đã chốt là markdown + examples (framing Q14) |
| Phương án mới, mở lại quyết định đã chốt | Bước này là đóng gói. Nếu viết lại phát hiện mâu thuẫn, ghi thành câu hỏi cho owner, không tự sửa quyết định |
| Dịch `work/` sang tiếng Anh | Rule 3 chỉ yêu cầu `## English summary` |
| CI cho chính repo nộp bài (workflow chạy `validate.sh`) | Thêm việc, ít giá trị cho người chấm; output kiểm được dán vào `examples/README.md` |

---

## 5. Câu hỏi cho owner

| # | Câu hỏi | Đề xuất |
|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Framework: (a) giữ ~11k từ, chỉ sửa link; (b) rút còn ~8k bằng cách chuyển rollout và evidence chi tiết sang file riêng; (c) tách thành 8 file theo layer | **(b).** (a) để người đọc tự lọc; (c) phá vỡ mọi tham chiếu "layer N" trong ADR, threat model, map và tốn nhiều vòng review |
| Q2 | Có viết `02-engineer-guide.md` không? | **Có**, ~1 200 từ, chỉ trình bày lại. Là mục đầu tiên cắt nếu thiếu thời gian |
| Q3 | Đổi tên docs sang tiền tố số (`01-framework.md` …) theo quy ước của repo? | **Có.** Việc cơ học, kiểm bằng grep link; ADR giữ tên vì đã có số riêng |
| Q4 | Phạm vi examples: Tier A + B, Tier C bỏ? | **Có** |
| Q5 | Cho phép cài `actionlint`, `zizmor` (và thử `parliament`) cục bộ — tải binary/pip, không chạm hạ tầng? | **Có**, cài vào scratch / venv riêng, không cài global |

You are an independent reviewer. Repo: /home/do.hoang.minh.hung/papaya-devsecops-challenge (a design submission for a DevSecOps hiring challenge; read CLAUDE.md first for the repo rules, especially Rule 1 evidence markers, Rule 3 language, Rule 4 "design, don't execute").

File under review: work/05-deliverable-plan.md (Vietnamese working note with an English summary). It decides what the final submission contains: list of docs, writing order, list of example config files in examples/ with how each is validated locally, and what is deliberately excluded.

1. Factual accuracy: every claim about the existing files, research rows, owner decisions (OD/D/framing Q), tool capabilities is correct and correctly marked (✅/📖/⚠️). Flag any claim that cites a research row that does not say that.
2. Completeness vs the brief and the framework: is anything the framework promises, or the challenge needs, missing from the submission list? Is anything in the plan redundant or likely to dilute the submission?
3. Consistency with approved decisions: does any proposed doc or example contradict an owner decision or the design (e.g. GitHub plan assumptions, approval gate, phases)?
4. Examples: does each one really prove the framework claim stated, and is the proposed validation actually local, feasible and honest about its limits? Are there validation claims that overstate what the check proves?
5. Writing order: is the stated dependency reasoning sound?
6. Rule compliance: no secrets/PII, language rules, Rule 4 (no live infra).

You may run local read-only commands (grep, wc, jq, curl to read public docs) to verify. Do not edit any file.

Output: a list of findings, each with severity HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW, location (section/row in the plan), the problem, evidence (file:line or command output), and a suggested fix. Then a one-line verdict. Write the report in English, concise.

## 3. Config mẫu trong `examples/`

Nguyên tắc chọn: mỗi file phải (1) chứng minh một claim cụ thể trong framework hoặc ADR, và (2) kiểm được
**cục bộ**, không chạm hạ tầng thật (Rule 4). Mỗi kiểm tra ghi rõ nó **không** chứng minh điều gì.

Quy ước chung:
- Placeholder (`<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>`, `123456789012`, `<org>`, `<ORG_ID>`…); comment đầu file trỏ về layer/ADR,
  phase áp dụng, và marker cho trường/khóa chưa kiểm.
- Test viết bằng Python `unittest` (✅ có sẵn; `pytest` chưa cài ✅), đặt trong `examples/tests/`.
- `examples/validate.sh` chạy mọi kiểm tra; output thật dán vào `examples/README.md` (✅).

# 05 — Kế hoạch deliverable (chốt sẽ nộp gì)

## English summary

- **Purpose:** fix exactly what is submitted before the final writing pass. No new design decisions here;
  this note only decides form, order, length and scope.
- **Docs (§1):** a one-page `README.md`, then numbered docs: framework (trimmed from ~11k to ~9.5–10k words by
  moving the rollout and evidence detail out, keeping a one-line evidence summary per layer), a new short
  engineer guide, rollout plan 30/60/90, a compliance "control and evidence register", the existing threat
  model and problem→control map, the 10 existing ADRs, and three Mermaid diagrams.
- **Writing order (§2):** change workflow (layer 3) and identity & access (layer 1) first, each written
  together with its examples; layer 5 is frozen input for them; supporting docs after; README last.
- **Examples (§3):** 8 core and 3 secondary artifacts, each tied to a framework claim and a local check whose
  limits are stated. Main pushback on the initial idea: "environment approval" does not exist for private
  repos on GitHub Team (R3.1.2), so the gate example is a **ruleset on `main`** plus an environment limited to
  `main` without reviewers; an IAM permission set alone proves little, so the OIDC trust policy (immutable
  `sub` format) and an SCP are added; the risk stop, the least proven part of the design, gets a runnable
  classifier; "CrossGuard" is now called Pulumi Policies and is a phase-2, secondary item.
- **Excluded (§4):** anything that would need invented facts (k0s, Firebase, GCP), running tools against real
  targets, implementations of open gaps, new decisions, and — pending the owner — a managed hook example.
- **Open questions (§5):** framework length, engineer guide, renaming docs, examples scope, installing
  linters/packages, dropping hooks from framing Q14, status of the problem→control map.
- Reviewed once by an independent agent (1 HIGH, 9 MEDIUM, all fixed; log in §6).

3	## English summary
4	
5	- **Purpose:** fix exactly what is submitted before the final writing pass. No new design decisions here;
6	  this note only decides form, order, length and scope.
7	- **Docs (§1):** a one-page `README.md`, then numbered docs: framework (trimmed from ~11k to ~9.5–10k words by
8	  moving the rollout and evidence detail out, keeping a one-line evidence summary per layer), a new short
9	  engineer guide, rollout plan 30/60/90, a compliance "control and evidence register", the existing threat
10	  model and problem→control map, the 10 existing ADRs, and three Mermaid diagrams.
11	- **Writing order (§2):** change workflow (layer 3) and identity & access (layer 1) first, each written
12	  together with its examples; layer 5 is frozen input for them; supporting docs after; README last.
13	- **Examples (§3):** 8 core and 3 secondary artifacts, each tied to a framework claim and a local check whose
14	  limits are stated. Main pushback on the initial idea: "environment approval" does not exist for private
15	  repos on GitHub Team (R3.1.2), so the gate example is a **ruleset on `main`** plus an environment limited to
16	  `main` without reviewers; an IAM permission set alone proves little, so the OIDC trust policy (immutable
17	  `sub` format) and an SCP are added; the risk stop, the least proven part of the design, gets a runnable
18	  classifier; "CrossGuard" is now called Pulumi Policies and is a phase-2, secondary item.
19	- **Excluded (§4):** anything that would need invented facts (k0s, Firebase, GCP), running tools against real
20	  targets, implementations of open gaps, new decisions, and — pending the owner — a managed hook example.

- **Purpose:** fix exactly what is submitted before the final writing pass. No new design decisions here;
  this note only decides form, order, length and scope.

  moving the rollout and evidence detail out, keeping a one-line evidence summary per layer), a new short
  engineer guide, rollout plan 30/60/90, a compliance "control and evidence register", the existing threat
  model and problem→control map, the 10 existing ADRs, and three Mermaid diagrams.
- **Writing order (§2):** change workflow (layer 3) and identity & access (layer 1) first, each written
  together with its examples; layer 5 is frozen input for them; supporting docs after; README last.
- **Examples (§3):** 8 core and 3 secondary artifacts, each tied to a framework claim and a local check whose
  limits are stated. Main pushback on the initial idea: "environment approval" does not exist for private
  repos on GitHub Team (R3.1.2), so the gate example is a **ruleset on `main`** plus an environment limited to
  `main` without reviewers; an IAM permission set alone proves little, so the OIDC trust policy (immutable
  `sub` format) and an SCP are added; the risk stop, the least proven part of the design, gets a runnable
  classifier; "CrossGuard" is now called Pulumi Policies and is a phase-2, secondary item.
- **Excluded (§4):** anything that would need invented facts (k0s, Firebase, GCP), running tools against real
  targets, implementations of open gaps, new decisions, and — pending the owner — a managed hook example.
- **Open questions (§5):** framework length, engineer guide, renaming docs, examples scope, installing
  linters/packages, dropping hooks from framing Q14, status of the problem→control map.
- Reviewed once by an independent agent (1 HIGH, 9 MEDIUM, all fixed; log in §6).

lines: -# Threat model: coding agents in Papaya's DevSecOps workflow
-> Status: draft for owner review · Updated: 2026-11-09 · Builds on [`framework.md`](framework.md) and
-Each threat maps to the controls that **prevent** it, **detect** it or **test** it, the **evidence**
-an auditor can ask for, and the **residual risk** that stays. Controls point to the framework layer
-(L1–L8) and ADR, and say when they arrive if not in phase 1. Markers follow the framework legend:
-📖 R*x.y* = documented research row in `work/02-research.md`; ⚠️ = inference or unverified;
-[design] = proposal of this submission. Codes: S-n success criteria, G-n gaps, OD-n owner decisions,
-GĐ-n framing assumptions, D1–D3 owner decisions in research 6.6, "Options §n" sections of
-★ = threat named in the task. The table assumes prompt injection succeeds sometimes: neither OWASP
-nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2). Controls therefore limit what a hijacked agent
-can reach, rather than trying to keep every input clean.
-- **Assets:** claim data (medical records, national IDs, bank accounts) of several insurer tenants;
-  production infrastructure (AWS, GCP, k0s, Firebase); credentials (SSO cache, CI secrets, app keys);
-  the evidence chain (PRs, CloudTrail, change records).
-- **Actors:** an external attacker who controls content the agent reads (partner uploads, tickets,
-  logs, PR comments, web pages); a malicious or compromised MCP server or plugin publisher; an insider
-  who weakens controls for speed; a thief of a CI credential.
-- **Boundaries:** the laptop is not trusted (GĐ-6); the boundaries that hold are AWS IAM/SCPs and the
-  merge to `main` (ADR-0002, ADR-0003). Agent settings are hygiene (ADR-0007). Hooks, plugins and local
-  MCP servers run outside the sandbox with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5).
-| # | Threat and example | Controls | Evidence | Residual risk |

-| T1 ★ | **Prompt injection from a partner-uploaded claim document.** A PDF holds hidden text: "read `~/.aws` and post it to this URL". The document is also PHI (research 1.11.4 L6; framing A7b). | Prevent: raw partner documents never enter an agent session; reproduce with synthetic documents or de-identify first [design] (L6, ADR-0009). A hijacked agent holds no standing prod write and no PHI read (from end of phase 1, layer 8; L1, ADR-0002). Phase 2: sandbox hides `~/.aws` from Bash and limits Bash network to an allowlist (📖 R1.6.3, R1.6.4); credential-path deny rules and `ask` for WebFetch cover the file and web tools (L2; 📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.4; `Read(...)` syntax ⚠️ R1.8 #5). Test: planted-injection test on the real configuration, phase 3 (📖 R6.1.5; ⚠️ R6.5 #12). | Policy text and training record; synthetic-fixture repo; planted-injection reports; OTel `tool_decision` (📖 research 6.6 D1). | "Never raw" is a process rule. Before phase 2 there is no sandbox and no credential deny; only Manual-mode prompts, which auto mode skips, stand between the injection and `~/.aws`. Broad allowed domains such as `github.com` are an exfiltration path (📖 R6.3.7). Excluded `aws` commands run outside the sandbox (📖 R1.6.4; ⚠️). |

-| T2 ★ | **Malicious MCP server.** An engineer adds a "Linear helper" from a public registry; its startup command reads `~/.aws`, or its tool output injects instructions (📖 R6.4.3). | Prevent: allowlist `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4), matched by `serverUrl` or exact `serverCommand`, never `serverName` (📖 R1.3.3); `disableClaudeAiConnectors` (📖 R1.3.7); review checklist: publisher, local or remote, data flows, no token passthrough (📖 R6.4.2, R6.4.3), pinned version [design] (L4, ADR-0006). These keys are in the phase-1 subset (may slip to phase 2 with the catalogue, owner agreement needed, layer 8). CI fixes its own MCP set, because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs (📖 R1.3.5). | Catalogue file in git with approving PRs; supplier register; monthly export of the console settings diffed with git (G18). | An approved local server runs outside the sandbox (📖 R1.6.2). Tool descriptions can change after approval (⚠️). Without MDM, another login skips server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11). |

-| T3 ★ | **Internal plugin sends data out.** A plugin in Papaya's marketplace gets an update whose hook posts transcripts to an outside endpoint. | Prevent: the main control is review of the update in the marketplace repo, which has its own ruleset and CODEOWNERS [design], with sources pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b) so an update needs a new reviewed pin. Only Papaya's marketplace is allowed (`strictKnownMarketplaces`, `blockedMarketplaces`, 📖 R1.4.2; phase 1, may slip with the catalogue); version floor covering the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7). Phase 2: `allowManagedHooksOnly` blocks hooks of plugins that are not force-enabled (📖 R1.5.4). Detect: OTel `plugin_installed` / `plugin_loaded` show which plugin version ran, not what it sent (📖 R1.4.6). | Marketplace PR history; catalogue entries; OTel plugin events; supplier register. | Hooks and plugin code run outside the sandbox with full network and the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5): no technical egress control applies. -## What the controls do not cover
-- **Process-only controls:** raw partner documents kept out of agent sessions (T1); no agent in the JIT
-  or PHI terminal (T6, T14); agents never approve PRs on laptops (T7); tenant posting rule (T6); incident-session flags (T19). They
-  rely on training and are checked by sampling, not enforced.
-- **Code outside the sandbox:** hooks, plugins and local MCP servers are limited only by review before
-  approval (T2, T3); excluded commands (`aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless`) only by prompts in Manual mode or
-  the classifier in auto mode (T1, T10).
-- **Laptops without MDM:** server-managed settings can be skipped (T2–T4; G11). The IAM and merge-gate
-- **k0s, GCP and Firebase:** same principles, mechanisms open (G1–G3); no risk stop, no break-glass,
-  no detection of a leaked deploy token.
-- **Phase 1 window:** until phase 2 there is no sandbox, no credential deny rules, no
-  `allowManagedHooksOnly`, no `allowedProviders`, no SCPs, no audit-log alerts and no policy checks
-  (T1, T3–T5, T10, T12–T14, T17). Standing prod write stays until its prerequisites are in place (layer 8).

+Each threat maps to the controls that **prevent** it, **detect** it or **test** it, the **evidence**

+[design] = proposal of this submission. Codes: S-n success criteria, G-n gaps, OD-n owner decisions,

+★ = threat named in the task. The table assumes prompt injection succeeds sometimes: neither OWASP
+nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2). Controls therefore limit what a hijacked agent
+can reach, rather than trying to keep every input clean.
+- **Assets:** claim data (medical records, national IDs, bank accounts) of several insurer tenants;
+  production infrastructure (AWS, GCP, k0s, Firebase); credentials (SSO cache, CI secrets, app keys);
+  the evidence chain (PRs, CloudTrail, change records).

+  logs, PR comments, web pages); a malicious or compromised MCP server or plugin publisher; an insider
+  who weakens controls for speed; a thief of a CI credential.
+- **Boundaries:** the laptop is not trusted (GĐ-6); the boundaries that hold are AWS IAM/SCPs and the
+  merge to `main` (ADR-0002, ADR-0003). Agent settings are hygiene (ADR-0007). Hooks, plugins and local
+  MCP servers run outside the sandbox with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5).

A CODEOWNERS file uses a pattern that follows most of the same rules used in [gitignore](https://git-scm.com/docs/gitignore#_pattern_format) files. The pattern is followed by one or more {% data variables.product.prodname_dotcom %} usernames or team names usin

{% ifversion enterprise-teams %}

> [!NOTE]
> When using teams, only organization teams can be code owners. Enterprise teams are not supported as code owners. See [AUTOTITLE](/admin/concepts/enterprise-fundamentals/teams-in-an-enterprise).

{% endif %}

If you want to match two or more code owners with the same pattern, all the code owners must be on the same line. If the code owners are not on the same line, the pattern matches only the last mentioned code owner.

{% ifversion fpt or ghec %}In most cases, you{% else %}You{% endif %} can also refer to a user by an email address that has been added to their account, for example `user@example.com`. {% ifversion fpt or ghec %} You cannot use an email address to refer to a {

CODEOWNERS paths are case sensitive, because {% data variables.product.prodname_dotcom %} uses a case sensitive file system. Since CODEOWNERS are evaluated by {% data variables.product.prodname_dotcom %}, even systems that are case insensitive (for example, ma

If any line in your CODEOWNERS file contains invalid syntax, that line will be skipped. When you navigate to the CODEOWNERS file in your repository, you can see any errors highlighted. A list of errors in a repository's CODEOWNERS file is also accessible via t

If you specify a user or team that doesn't exist or has insufficient access, a code owner will not be assigned.

### Example of a CODEOWNERS file

```text
# This is a comment.
# Each line is a file pattern followed by one or more owners.

# These owners will be the default owners for everything in
# the repo. Unless a later match takes precedence,
# @global-owner1 and @global-owner2 will be requested for
# review when someone opens a pull request.
*       @global-owner1 @global-owner2

# Order is important; the last matching pattern takes the most
# precedence. When someone opens a pull request that only
# modifies JS files, only @js-owner and not the global
# owner(s) will be requested for a review.
*.js    @js-owner #This is an inline comment.

# You can also use email addresses if you prefer. They'll be
# used to look up users just like we do for commit author
# emails.
*.go docs@example.com

# Teams can be specified as code owners as well. Teams should
# be identified in the format @org/team-name. Teams must have
# explicit write access to the repository. In this example,
# the octocats team in the octo-org organization owns all .txt files.
*.txt @octo-org/octocats

# In this example, @doctocat owns any files in the build/logs
# directory at the root of the repository and any of its
# subdirectories.
/build/logs/ @doctocat

# The `docs/*` pattern will match files like
# `docs/getting-started.md` but not further nested files like
# `docs/build-app/troubleshooting.md`.
docs/* docs@example.com

# In this example, @octocat owns any file in an apps directory
# anywhere in your repository.
apps/ @octocat

# In this example, @doctocat owns any file in the `/docs`
# directory in the root of your repository and any of its
# subdirectories.
/docs/ @doctocat

# In this example, any change inside the `/scripts` directory
# will require approval from @doctocat or @octocat.
/scripts/ @doctocat @octocat

# In this example, @octocat owns any file in a `/logs` directory such as
# `/build/logs`, `/scripts/logs`, and `/deeply/nested/logs`. Any changes
# in a `/logs` directory will require approval from @octocat.
**/logs @octocat

# In this example, @octocat owns any file in the `/apps`
# directory in the root of your repository except for the `/apps/github`
# subdirectory, as its owners are left empty. Without an owner, changes
# to `apps/github` can be made with the approval of any user who has
# write access to the repository.
/apps/ @octocat
/apps/github

# In this example, @octocat owns any file in the `/apps`
# directory in the root of your repository except for the `/apps/github`
# subdirectory, as this subdirectory has its own owner @doctocat
/apps/ @octocat
/apps/github @doctocat
```

"""E2: CODEOWNERS gives each path the owners the framework requires.

Resolves the *effective* owners of sample paths with GitHub's rule "the last matching
pattern takes the most precedence" (GitHub docs, about-code-owners), so a broad line
placed after the L3 section would make this test fail.

The pattern matcher implements the gitignore subset CODEOWNERS supports: leading `/`
anchors to the root, trailing `/` matches a directory and everything below it, `*`
does not cross `/`, `**` does, and a pattern with no inner `/` matches at any depth.
It is checked against the examples in GitHub's docs (MatcherTest). It is a model of
GitHub's behaviour, not GitHub itself.

Not checked (needs the real repository): that teams exist and have write access.
GitHub skips such owners silently.
"""
import os
import re
import unittest

HERE = os.path.dirname(__file__)
CODEOWNERS = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "github", "CODEOWNERS")

L3 = "@example-org/l3-owners"
ONCALL = "@example-org/oncall-approvers"

# Canonical L3 path list, framework layer 5 "CODEOWNERS" bullet, one sample file each.
PROCESS_L3_SAMPLES = [
    ".github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml",
    ".github/CODEOWNERS",
    "CLAUDE.md",
    "services/claims/CLAUDE.md",        # nested CLAUDE.md inside a domain path
    "CLAUDE.local.md",
    ".claude/settings.json",
    "services/claims/.claude/settings.json",
    ".claude.json",
    ".mcp.json",
    "services/claims/.mcp.json",
    ".husky/pre-commit",
    ".gitmodules",
    ".ripgreprc",
    ".devcontainer/devcontainer.json",
    ".npmrc",
    "services/claims/.npmrc",
    "policy-packs/aws/index.ts",
    "infra/pulumi/org-scp/index.ts",
    "agent-config/managed-settings.json",
]

# Deployable paths: (sample file, domain team that must be an owner).
DEPLOYABLE_SAMPLES = [
    ("services/claims/serverless.yml", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("services/claims/src/handler.ts", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("services/underwriting/serverless.yml", "@example-org/team-underwriting"),
    ("web/firebase.json", "@example-org/team-web"),
    ("infra/pulumi/claims-data/index.ts", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("k8s/claims/deployment.yaml", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("infra/pulumi/iam/index.ts", L3),
]

RISK_STOP_SAMPLES = [
    ("deploy-approvals/claims-data/0123abcd.yaml", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("deploy-approvals/iam/0123abcd.yaml", L3),
]


def pattern_to_regex(pattern):
    anchored = pattern.startswith("/")
    p = pattern.lstrip("/")
    directory = p.endswith("/")
    p = p.rstrip("/")
    if "/" in p:
        anchored = True  # gitignore: a slash in the middle anchors the pattern
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(p):
        if p.startswith("**/", i):
            out += "(?:.*/)?"
            i += 3
        elif p.startswith("**", i):
            out += ".*"
            i += 2
        elif p[i] == "*":
            out += "[^/]*"
            i += 1
        elif p[i] == "?":
            out += "[^/]"
            i += 1
        else:
            out += re.escape(p[i])
            i += 1
    prefix = "^" if anchored else "^(?:.*/)?"
    # A file pattern also matches a directory of that name (and its contents);
    # a directory pattern matches only contents.
    suffix = "/.*$" if directory else "(?:/.*)?$"
    return re.compile(prefix + out + suffix)


def parse(path):
    rules = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for n, line in enumerate(f, 1):
            line = line.split(" #")[0].strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            parts = line.split()
            rules.append((n, parts[0], parts[1:]))
    return rules


def owners_of(rules, path):
    result = None
    for _, pattern, owners in rules:
        if pattern_to_regex(pattern).match(path):
            result = owners
    return result


class MatcherTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """The matcher against the examples in GitHub's CODEOWNERS docs."""

    def test_docs_examples(self):
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("*.js").match("a/b/c.js"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("/build/logs/").match("build/logs/x/y.log"))
        self.assertFalse(pattern_to_regex("/build/logs/").match("src/build/logs/y.log"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("docs/*").match("docs/getting-started.md"))
        self.assertFalse(pattern_to_regex("docs/*").match("docs/build-app/troubleshooting.md"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("apps/").match("x/apps/y.js"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("**/logs").match("deeply/nested/logs/a"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("/apps/github").match("apps/github/a.js"))

    def test_last_match_wins(self):
        rules = [(1, "/apps/", ["@octocat"]), (2, "/apps/github", ["@doctocat"])]
        self.assertEqual(owners_of(rules, "apps/github/x"), ["@doctocat"])
        self.assertEqual(owners_of(rules, "apps/other/x"), ["@octocat"])

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):

    def test_syntax(self):

            with self.subTest(line=n):
                self.assertNotIn("!", pattern, "negation does not work in CODEOWNERS")
                self.assertNotRegex(pattern, r"\[", "character ranges do not work in CODEOWNERS")
                self.assertTrue(owners, "a pattern without owners removes ownership")
                for o in owners:
                    self.assertRegex(o, r"^@[\w.-]+/[\w.-]+$", "owners must be org teams")

    def test_process_paths_only_l3_team(self):
        for path in PROCESS_L3_SAMPLES:
            with self.subTest(path=path):
                self.assertEqual(owners_of(self.rules, path), [L3])

    def test_deployable_paths_domain_plus_oncall(self):
        for path, team in DEPLOYABLE_SAMPLES:
            with self.subTest(path=path):
                owners = owners_of(self.rules, path)
                self.assertIsNotNone(owners, "unowned deployable path: any writer could approve")
                self.assertIn(team, owners)
                self.assertIn(ONCALL, owners)

    def test_risk_stop_approvals_stack_owners_plus_oncall(self):
        for path, team in RISK_STOP_SAMPLES:
            with self.subTest(path=path):
                self.assertEqual(sorted(owners_of(self.rules, path)), sorted([team, ONCALL]))

    def test_oncall_never_on_process_paths(self):
        for _, pattern, owners in self.rules:
            if L3 in owners and ONCALL not in owners:
                continue
            for path in PROCESS_L3_SAMPLES:
                if pattern_to_regex(pattern).match(path):
                    # allowed only if a later L3-only line overrides it (checked above)
                    self.assertEqual(owners_of(self.rules, path), [L3])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""E2: CODEOWNERS gives each path the owners the framework requires.

Resolves the *effective* owners of sample paths with GitHub's rule "the last matching
pattern takes the most precedence" (GitHub docs, about-code-owners), so a broad line
placed after the L3 section would make this test fail.

The pattern matcher implements the gitignore subset CODEOWNERS supports: leading `/`
anchors to the root, trailing `/` matches a directory and everything below it, `*`
does not cross `/`, `**` does, and a pattern with no inner `/` matches at any depth.
It is checked against the examples in GitHub's docs (MatcherTest). It is a model of
GitHub's behaviour, not GitHub itself.

Not checked (needs the real repository): that teams exist and have write access.
GitHub skips such owners silently.
"""
import os
import re
import unittest

HERE = os.path.dirname(__file__)
CODEOWNERS = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "github", "CODEOWNERS")

L3 = "@example-org/l3-owners"
ONCALL = "@example-org/oncall-approvers"

# Canonical L3 path list, framework layer 5 "CODEOWNERS" bullet, one sample file each.
PROCESS_L3_SAMPLES = [
    ".github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml",
    ".github/CODEOWNERS",
    "CLAUDE.md",
    "services/claims/CLAUDE.md",        # nested CLAUDE.md inside a domain path
    "CLAUDE.local.md",
    ".claude/settings.json",
    "services/claims/.claude/settings.json",
    ".claude.json",
    ".mcp.json",
    "services/claims/.mcp.json",
    ".husky/pre-commit",
    ".gitmodules",
    ".ripgreprc",
    ".devcontainer/devcontainer.json",
    ".npmrc",
    "services/claims/.npmrc",
    "policy-packs/aws/index.ts",
    "infra/pulumi/org-scp/index.ts",
    "agent-config/managed-settings.json",
]

# Deployable paths: (sample file, domain team that must be an owner).
DEPLOYABLE_SAMPLES = [
    ("services/claims/serverless.yml", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("services/claims/src/handler.ts", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("services/underwriting/serverless.yml", "@example-org/team-underwriting"),
    ("web/firebase.json", "@example-org/team-web"),
    ("infra/pulumi/claims-data/index.ts", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("k8s/claims/deployment.yaml", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("infra/pulumi/iam/index.ts", L3),
]

RISK_STOP_SAMPLES = [
    ("deploy-approvals/claims-data/0123abcd.yaml", "@example-org/team-claims"),
    ("deploy-approvals/iam/0123abcd.yaml", L3),
]


def pattern_to_regex(pattern):
    anchored = pattern.startswith("/")
    p = pattern.lstrip("/")
    directory = p.endswith("/")
    p = p.rstrip("/")
    if "/" in p:
        anchored = True  # gitignore: a slash in the middle anchors the pattern
    out = ""
    i = 0
    while i < len(p):
        if p.startswith("**/", i):
            out += "(?:.*/)?"
            i += 3
        elif p.startswith("**", i):
            out += ".*"
            i += 2
        elif p[i] == "*":
            out += "[^/]*"
            i += 1
        elif p[i] == "?":
            out += "[^/]"
            i += 1
        else:
            out += re.escape(p[i])
            i += 1
    prefix = "^" if anchored else "^(?:.*/)?"
    # A file pattern also matches a directory of that name (and its contents);
    # a directory pattern matches only contents.
    suffix = "/.*$" if directory else "(?:/.*)?$"
    return re.compile(prefix + out + suffix)


def parse(path):
    rules = []
    with open(path) as f:
        for n, line in enumerate(f, 1):
            line = line.split(" #")[0].strip()
            if not line or line.startswith("#"):
                continue
            parts = line.split()
            rules.append((n, parts[0], parts[1:]))
    return rules


def owners_of(rules, path):
    result = None
    for _, pattern, owners in rules:
        if pattern_to_regex(pattern).match(path):
            result = owners
    return result


class MatcherTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """The matcher against the examples in GitHub's CODEOWNERS docs."""

    def test_docs_examples(self):
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("*.js").match("a/b/c.js"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("/build/logs/").match("build/logs/x/y.log"))
        self.assertFalse(pattern_to_regex("/build/logs/").match("src/build/logs/y.log"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("docs/*").match("docs/getting-started.md"))
        self.assertFalse(pattern_to_regex("docs/*").match("docs/build-app/troubleshooting.md"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("apps/").match("x/apps/y.js"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("**/logs").match("deeply/nested/logs/a"))
        self.assertTrue(pattern_to_regex("/apps/github").match("apps/github/a.js"))

    def test_last_match_wins(self):
        rules = [(1, "/apps/", ["@octocat"]), (2, "/apps/github", ["@doctocat"])]
        self.assertEqual(owners_of(rules, "apps/github/x"), ["@doctocat"])
        self.assertEqual(owners_of(rules, "apps/other/x"), ["@octocat"])


class CodeownersTest(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.rules = parse(CODEOWNERS)

    def test_syntax(self):
        for n, pattern, owners in self.rules:
            with self.subTest(line=n):
                self.assertNotIn("!", pattern, "negation does not work in CODEOWNERS")
                self.assertNotRegex(pattern, r"\[", "character ranges do not work in CODEOWNERS")
                self.assertTrue(owners, "a pattern without owners removes ownership")
                for o in owners:
                    self.assertRegex(o, r"^@[\w.-]+/[\w.-]+$", "owners must be org teams")

    def test_process_paths_only_l3_team(self):
        for path in PROCESS_L3_SAMPLES:
            with self.subTest(path=path):
                self.assertEqual(owners_of(self.rules, path), [L3])

    def test_deployable_paths_domain_plus_oncall(self):
        for path, team in DEPLOYABLE_SAMPLES:
            with self.subTest(path=path):
                owners = owners_of(self.rules, path)
                self.assertIsNotNone(owners, "unowned deployable path: any writer could approve")
                self.assertIn(team, owners)
                self.assertIn(ONCALL, owners)

    def test_risk_stop_approvals_stack_owners_plus_oncall(self):
        for path, team in RISK_STOP_SAMPLES:
            with self.subTest(path=path):
                self.assertEqual(sorted(owners_of(self.rules, path)), sorted([team, ONCALL]))

    def test_oncall_never_on_process_paths(self):
        for _, pattern, owners in self.rules:
            if L3 in owners and ONCALL not in owners:
                continue
            for path in PROCESS_L3_SAMPLES:
                if pattern_to_regex(pattern).match(path):
                    # allowed only if a later L3-only line overrides it (checked above)
                    self.assertEqual(owners_of(self.rules, path), [L3])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
