# Reusable production deploy (framework layer 3 "Merge approval = deploy approval", layer 5).
# The ONLY workflow that references the `production` environment. Called by deploy-on-main.yml.
#
# Conditions this file must keep (checked by examples/tests/test_workflow_policy.py):
# - no ref/SHA input: it deploys the commit that was merged (github.sha of the push to main);
# - one concurrency group per stack, never cancel-in-progress (Pulumi guide: cancelling can
#   leave infrastructure half-applied);
# - OIDC only (id-token: write); no AWS keys; every action pinned to a full commit SHA;
# - prod preview -> risk stop -> apply. No --skip-preview, --target, --replace, state, import, destroy.
#
# Repository variables (not secrets): AWS_REGION, PROD_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, PULUMI_BACKEND_URL,
# PULUMI_CLI_VERSION, NODE_VERSION.
name: deploy-prod

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      stack:
        description: Stack name, e.g. claims-data. Also the deploy-approvals/<stack>/ directory.
        type: string
        required: true
      tool:
        description: "pulumi or serverless"
        type: string
        required: true
      workdir:
        description: Directory of the stack in the monorepo
        type: string
        required: true

permissions: {}

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment: production
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-prod-${{ inputs.stack }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      STACK: ${{ inputs.stack }}
      TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
      WORKDIR: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
      PREVIEW: ${{ runner.temp }}/preview.json
    steps:
      - name: Check out the merged commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ vars.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: AWS credentials through GitHub OIDC (no stored keys)
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd # v6.3.0
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.PROD_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}
          # The run ID in the session name links CloudTrail events to this run (layer 7 change record).
          role-session-name: deploy-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}

      # ---------------- Pulumi ----------------
      - name: Install the Pulumi CLI only
        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
        uses: pulumi/actions@8e5e406f4007fca908480587cb9893c07090f58d # v7.0.0
        with:
          pulumi-version: ${{ vars.PULUMI_CLI_VERSION }}

      - name: Preview prod (Pulumi)
        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
        env:
          PULUMI_BACKEND_URL: ${{ vars.PULUMI_BACKEND_URL }}
        run: |
          npm ci
          pulumi preview --stack "$STACK" --json > "$PREVIEW"

# Required check `codeowners-validate` (ruleset-main.json; framework layer 5).
# GitHub silently skips invalid CODEOWNERS lines and owners that do not exist or lack write
# access, so a typo can remove an approval requirement without anyone noticing. This job fails
# the PR when GitHub reports any CODEOWNERS error for the PR's head commit.
# Note: GitHub applies the CODEOWNERS file of the BASE branch to a PR; this check stops a broken
# file from reaching main in the first place.
name: codeowners-validate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  codeowners-validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Ask GitHub for CODEOWNERS errors
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          errors=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/codeowners/errors?ref=$HEAD_SHA" --jq '.errors | length')
          if [ "$errors" != "0" ]; then
            gh api "repos/$REPO/codeowners/errors?ref=$HEAD_SHA" --jq '.errors[] | "line \(.line): \(.kind) \(.message)"'
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "CODEOWNERS: no errors"

# Required check `codeowners-validate` (ruleset-main.json; framework layer 5).
# GitHub silently skips invalid CODEOWNERS lines and owners that do not exist or lack write
# access, so a typo can remove an approval requirement without anyone noticing. This job fails
# the PR when GitHub reports any CODEOWNERS error for the PR's head commit.
# Note: GitHub applies the CODEOWNERS file of the BASE branch to a PR; this check stops a broken
# file from reaching main in the first place.
name: codeowners-validate

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  codeowners-validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Ask GitHub for CODEOWNERS errors
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          errors=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/codeowners/errors?ref=$HEAD_SHA" --jq '.errors | length')
          if [ "$errors" != "0" ]; then
            gh api "repos/$REPO/codeowners/errors?ref=$HEAD_SHA" --jq '.errors[] | "line \(.line): \(.kind) \(.message)"'
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "CODEOWNERS: no errors"

v1.30.0

❌
Detects uses of in-repo actions or reusable workflows that don't use GitHub's
dedicated "self-repository" syntax.
As of July 2026, GitHub supports a new "self-repository" syntax
(uses: $/...) when referring to actions or reusable workflows
within uses: clauses.
This syntax has security and policy enforcement benefits when compared to
the old "workspace-relative" (uses: ./...) syntax:
Unlike the "workspace-relative" form, the "self-repository" form is not subject
  to runtime filesystem state, meaning that it can't load an action that was
  cloned at runtime in a previous step.
Using the "self-repository" form makes it possible to enforce a "fully pinned"
  policy on GitHub itself, as the "self-repository" form is treated as a form
  pinning whereas the "workspace-relative" form is not.
Other resources:
GitHub Blog: Reference same-repository actions with self-repository syntax
Bypassing GitHub Actions policies in the dumbest way possible
Remediation🔗
Replace any workspace-relative uses: clause with its self-repository equivalent.
For example:
Example
Before After 
self-repository.ymljobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: ./my-action
self-repository.ymljobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: $/my-action

# PR preview against NON-PROD only (framework layer 3, "Pulumi" bullet): a prod preview would run
# the PR's code with prod state-write and secret access. Prod is previewed only on main, in
# deploy-prod.yml, after the merge.
# The non-prod role trusts the `pull_request` subject of this repository; it has no prod access.
name: pr-preview-nonprod

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - stack: claims-data
            workdir: infra/pulumi/claims-data
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ vars.NODE_VERSION }}

      - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd # v6.3.0
        with:
          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.NONPROD_PREVIEW_ROLE_ARN }}
          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

      - uses: pulumi/actions@8e5e406f4007fca908480587cb9893c07090f58d # v7.0.0
        with:
          pulumi-version: ${{ vars.PULUMI_CLI_VERSION }}

      - name: Preview non-prod
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.workdir }}
        env:
          STACK: ${{ matrix.stack }}-nonprod
          PULUMI_BACKEND_URL: ${{ vars.NONPROD_PULUMI_BACKEND_URL }}
        run: |
          npm ci
          pulumi preview --stack "$STACK" --diff

classifier does not know. Advisory policy findings join in phase 2 (not implemented here).

Approval: the original author opens a PR adding deploy-approvals/<stack>/<commit>.yaml with

any change merged in between stops it again (Options §1).

is posted shows type, name and operation only: no property values, outputs or secrets.

                "detail_digest": "<sha256 of the changed values>"}]}

import hashlib
import json
import os
import re

    r"^(aws:rds/|aws:s3/bucket(V2)?:|aws:dynamodb/table|aws:efs/|aws:kms/key|aws:sqs/queue:"

    r"|AWS::RDS::|AWS::S3::Bucket$|AWS::DynamoDB::Table|AWS::EFS::|AWS::KMS::Key"
    r"|AWS::SQS::Queue$|AWS::ElastiCache::|AWS::SecretsManager::Secret$)"

    r"^(aws:iam/|aws:organizations/policy|aws:s3/bucketPolicy|aws:sqs/queuePolicy"
    r"|aws:lambda/permission|aws:kms/keyPolicy|aws:secretsmanager/secretPolicy"
    r"|AWS::IAM::|AWS::Organizations::Policy|AWS::S3::BucketPolicy|AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy"
    r"|AWS::Lambda::Permission|AWS::KMS::Key$)"
)

    r"^(aws:ec2/(securityGroup|vpc|subnet|routeTable|route:|internetGateway|natGateway"

    r"|AWS::EC2::(SecurityGroup|VPC|Subnet|RouteTable|Route$|InternetGateway|NatGateway"

            f.write(text)
    return code

"""E7: risk stop classifier (examples/risk-stop/).

Proves the [design] logic: what stops a deploy, that an approval matches only the exact
preview it was given for, and that the posted summary carries no property values.

Does NOT prove: the real JSON shape of `pulumi preview --json` / `serverless diff --json`
(adapters are ⚠️ assumptions, fixtures are hand-written), nor that a real preview gives the
same hash twice for the same code (⚠️ Options §8: unknown values, provider churn).
"""
import io
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stdout, redirect_stderr

HERE = os.path.dirname(__file__)
RS = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "risk-stop")
sys.path.insert(0, RS)
import classify  # noqa: E402


def fixture(name):
    return os.path.join(RS, "fixtures", name)


def run(tool, preview, approvals):
    out = io.StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(out), redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
        code = classify.main(["--tool", tool, "--preview", preview, "--approvals", approvals])
    return code, out.getvalue()


class RiskStopTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.empty = os.path.join(self.tmp, "none")
        self.approved = os.path.join(RS, "deploy-approvals", "claims-data")

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp)

    def write(self, name, obj):
        path = os.path.join(self.tmp, name)
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(obj, f)
        return path

    def test_benign_change_continues(self):
        code, out = run("normalized", fixture("normalized-benign.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)

    def test_lambda_version_churn_is_not_a_stateful_delete(self):
        c = {"type": "AWS::Lambda::Version", "name": "v", "op": "delete"}
        self.assertEqual(classify.reasons_for(c), [])

    def test_iam_change_stops(self):
        code, out = run("normalized", fixture("normalized-iam.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
        self.assertIn("IAM", out)

    def test_stateful_replace_stops(self):
        code, _ = run("normalized", fixture("normalized-stateful-delete.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)

    def test_network_change_stops(self):
        p = self.write("n.json", {"changes": [
            {"type": "aws:ec2/securityGroupRule:SecurityGroupRule", "name": "ingress", "op": "create"}]})
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", p, self.empty)[0], 3)

    def test_unknown_operation_stops(self):
        p = self.write("u.json", {"changes": [{"type": "aws:lambda/function:Function", "name": "f", "op": "import"}]})
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", p, self.empty)[0], 3)

    def test_unreadable_preview_fails_closed(self):
        p = os.path.join(self.tmp, "bad.json")
        with open(p, "w") as f:
            f.write("{not json")
        self.assertEqual(run("pulumi", p, self.empty)[0], 2)
        p2 = self.write("wrong.json", {"unexpected": []})
        self.assertEqual(run("pulumi", p2, self.empty)[0], 2)

    def test_matching_approval_continues(self):
        code, out = run("normalized", fixture("normalized-iam.json"), self.approved)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertIn("approved by", out)

    def test_approval_does_not_cover_a_different_iam_change(self):
        # Same resource, same operation, different policy content (A approved, B deployed).
        with open(fixture("normalized-iam.json")) as f:
            doc = json.load(f)
        doc["changes"][1]["detail_digest"] = "policy-version-B"
        p = self.write("b.json", doc)
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", p, self.approved)[0], 3)

    def test_change_merged_in_between_stops_again(self):
        with open(fixture("normalized-iam.json")) as f:
            doc = json.load(f)
        doc["changes"].append({"type": "aws:sqs/queue:Queue", "name": "x", "op": "update", "detail_digest": "z"})
        p = self.write("later.json", doc)
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", p, self.approved)[0], 3)

    def test_summary_has_no_property_values(self):
        code, out = run("pulumi", fixture("pulumi-preview.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)  # S3 bucket replaced
        self.assertNotIn("PLACEHOLDER-SECRET-LIKE-VALUE", out)
        self.assertNotIn("2048", out)

    def test_serverless_adapter_iam_stops(self):
        code, out = run("serverless", fixture("serverless-diff.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
        self.assertIn("AWS::IAM::Role", out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run every local check on examples/. Nothing here contacts AWS, GitHub settings or any
# other live system. Tools that are not installed are SKIPPED with a message, never
# reported as passed. Set ACTIONLINT / ZIZMOR to the binaries if they are not on PATH.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

ACTIONLINT="${ACTIONLINT:-actionlint}"
ZIZMOR="${ZIZMOR:-zizmor}"
fail=0
skipped=()

section() { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$1"; }
have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
run() { "$@" || { echo "FAILED: $*"; fail=1; }; }

section "tool versions"
python3 --version
python3 -c 'import jsonschema, yaml; print("jsonschema", jsonschema.__version__, "| PyYAML", yaml.__version__)'
for t in jq yamllint shellcheck "$ACTIONLINT" "$ZIZMOR"; do
  if have "$t"; then printf '%s: %s\n' "$(basename "$t")" "$("$t" --version 2>&1 | head -1)"
  else printf '%s: not installed\n' "$(basename "$t")"; fi
done

section "JSON syntax (jq)"
if have jq; then
  while IFS= read -r f; do run jq empty "$f"; done < <(find . -name '*.json' -not -path './*/node_modules/*' | sort)
  echo "checked $(find . -name '*.json' -not -path './*/node_modules/*' | wc -l) files"
else skipped+=("jq"); echo "SKIPPED: jq not installed"; fi

section "YAML style (yamllint)"
if have yamllint; then
  run yamllint -d '{extends: default, rules: {line-length: {max: 120}, document-start: disable, truthy: {check-keys: false}, comments: {min-spaces-from-content: 1}}}' github/workflows
else skipped+=("yamllint"); echo "SKIPPED: yamllint not installed"; fi

section "GitHub Actions (actionlint)"
if have "$ACTIONLINT"; then
  # actionlint 1.7.12 (latest, March 2026) predates GitHub's same-repository `$/` syntax for
  # reusable workflows (GitHub docs, workflow-syntax, jobs.<job_id>.uses). Only that message
  # is ignored.
  SC=(); have shellcheck && SC=(-shellcheck "$(command -v shellcheck)")
  run "$ACTIONLINT" "${SC[@]}" -ignore 'reusable workflow call "\$/' github/workflows/*.yml
  echo "actionlint done"
else skipped+=("actionlint"); echo "SKIPPED: actionlint not installed"; fi

section "GitHub Actions security (zizmor, offline, auditor persona)"
if have "$ZIZMOR"; then
  run "$ZIZMOR" --offline --no-progress --persona=auditor github/workflows/*.yml
else skipped+=("zizmor"); echo "SKIPPED: zizmor not installed"; fi

section "unit tests (python3 -m unittest)"
run python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -v

section "result"
if [ ${#skipped[@]} -gt 0 ]; then echo "SKIPPED (not verified): ${skipped[*]}"; fi
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then echo "RESULT: FAILED"; exit 1; fi
echo "RESULT: all executed checks passed"

# Examples

> Status: step 1 of the writing plan (change workflow, layer 3). Identity examples (E4–E6) and
> agent/supply-chain examples (E8–E10) follow. · Updated: 2026-11-09

Concrete files behind [`../docs/01-framework.md`](../docs/01-framework.md). Each one exists to
prove one claim of the framework, and each has a local check. **Nothing here was run against
GitHub, AWS or any live system.** A passing check shows that the file says what the framework
says; it does not show that the platform enforces it. Every check below lists what it does
**not** prove.

Placeholders: `example-org`, `<owner team>`, `123456` (app ID), `<AWS_ACCOUNT_ID>`. The monorepo
layout (`services/`, `infra/pulumi/`, `k8s/`, `web/`) is invented for the examples; Papaya's
real layout is unknown.

## How to run

```bash
examples/validate.sh            # skips tools that are not installed, and says so
ACTIONLINT=/path/actionlint ZIZMOR=/path/zizmor examples/validate.sh
```

Needs Python 3 with `jsonschema` and `PyYAML`; optional `jq`, `yamllint`, `shellcheck`,
`actionlint`, `zizmor`. Tests use the standard `unittest`.

## What each file proves

| # | Files | Proves (framework) | Checked by | Does not prove |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | [`github/ruleset-main.json`](github/ruleset-main.json) | The approval gate is the merge to `main` (layer 3, ADR-0003): PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, stale approvals dismissed, approval by someone other than the last pusher, branch up to date (no merge queue), required checks pinned to a source app, no force push or deletion, nobody on the bypass list | JSON Schema of the create-ruleset request body; key-by-path check; design tests | That GitHub enforces it. `approval-gate` comes from a dedicated app whose ID (`123456`) is a placeholder (gap G19). Other checks are pinned to GitHub Actions (ID 15368, from `GET /apps/github-actions`), which any workflow in the repo can impersonate by job name (layer 3) |
| E2 | [`github/CODEOWNERS`](github/CODEOWNERS) | L3 process paths are owned by the L3 owner team only; deployable paths by the domain team **and** the on-call approver group (OD9, OD13); risk-stop approvals by the stack's owners and on-call (OD8) | Effective owners of sample paths resolved with GitHub's "last matching pattern wins" rule; a mutation run (a broad line appended after the L3 section) makes 6 assertions fail | That the teams exist and have write access: GitHub drops such owners silently. The `codeowners-validate` workflow covers that in a real repo |
| E3 | [`github/workflows/`](github/workflows/) | "Merge approval = deploy approval" (layer 3): only the reusable [`deploy-prod.yml`](github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml) uses `production`; no ref/SHA input; no `workflow_dispatch`, `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run`; one concurrency group per stack, never cancelled; preview → risk stop → apply. Layer 5: OIDC, per-job permissions, SHA-pinned actions. PRs preview non-prod only | `actionlint`, `zizmor --persona=auditor`, `yamllint`, and design tests (`test_workflow_policy.py`) | That the workflows run: the Pulumi/Serverless steps were never executed. The tests see only these files, not a whole monorepo |
| E3b | [`github/environment-production/`](github/environment-production/) | `production` accepts deployments from `main` only and has no required reviewers (not available on GitHub Team for private repos, R3.1.2); holds only the names of the k0s/Firebase exception secrets (OD1, OD6) | JSON Schemas of the two request bodies (environment PUT, branch-policy POST); key-by-path check; design tests | That GitHub applies it; admins can still change or delete the environment (layer 7 compares live settings) |
| E7 | [`risk-stop/`](risk-stop/) | The risk stop (layer 3, ADR-0004) can be built: risky prod diffs stop the deploy; an approval matches only the exact preview it was given for; a change merged in between stops it again; the posted summary has no property values; unreadable input stops (fail closed) | 12 unit tests on hand-written fixtures | ⚠️ The JSON shapes of `pulumi preview --json` and `serverless diff --json` are **assumed** ([`adapters.py`](risk-stop/adapters.py)); no real output was available. That a real preview gives the same hash twice for unchanged code (Options §8) |

Schemas in [`schemas/`](schemas/) are extracted from GitHub's REST OpenAPI description
(`github/rest-api-description` at commit `2f8f80e47ea4d3292cf4e37ba9d9b25475e06140`, OpenAPI 3.0.3)
by [`tools/extract_github_schemas.py`](tools/extract_github_schemas.py), which resolves `$ref` and
`nullable`. They do not forbid unknown keys, so a misspelled key passes schema validation; the
key-by-path check ([`tests/schema_keys.py`](tests/schema_keys.py)) catches it. Shown by a mutation
run: `require_last_pusher_approval` passes the schema and is reported by the key check.

## Findings from writing these files

Writing the examples surfaced points the framework text does not yet say. They are listed here
and carried into the framework in the final pass.

1. **The risk-stop classifier must be an L3 path.** The deploy runs the classifier from the
   merged commit, so a PR that edits the classifier and an IAM policy together, approved by the
   domain team, would switch the stop off. [`CODEOWNERS`](github/CODEOWNERS) adds
   `/tools/risk-stop/` to the L3 owner team ([design]; not in the framework's layer-5 list yet).
2. **The approval hash must cover changed values, not only resource names.** Otherwise an
   approval for one IAM policy change would also let a different change to the same policy
   through. The hash includes a digest of the old and new inputs; the summary shows none of them.
3. **Serverless replaces `AWS::Lambda::Version` on every code change** (shown in the Serverless
   `diff` docs examples). The classifier does not count that as a stateful delete, or every
   deploy would stop.
4. **Same-repository reusable workflows can use `uses: $/.github/workflows/<file>`**, which
   GitHub now recommends: it always resolves to the running commit, not the runner's workspace
   (GitHub docs, workflow syntax `jobs.<job_id>.uses`; zizmor audit `self-repository`). The
   latest `actionlint` (1.7.12) does not know the syntax yet; `validate.sh` ignores only that message.
5. **`runner.temp` is not available in job-level `env`** (caught by `actionlint`); paths use
   `$RUNNER_TEMP` inside steps.

GitHub, AWS or any live system.** A passing check shows that the file says what the framework
says; it does not show that the platform enforces it. Every check below lists what it does
**not** prove.

layout (`services/`, `infra/pulumi/`, `k8s/`, `web/`) is invented for the examples; Papaya's
real layout is unknown.

```bash

ACTIONLINT=/path/actionlint ZIZMOR=/path/zizmor examples/validate.sh
```

  - **Problem:** the only check is the order of the step names.
  - **Evidence:** I made each of these changes alone, and each passed all 43 tests, actionlint and zizmor:
    - `continue-on-error: true` on the "Risk stop" step;
    - `python3 tools/risk-stop/classify.py || true; …`;
    - `if: always() && inputs.tool == 'pulumi'` on the Apply step.

    - overwrite `tools/risk-stop/classify.py`;
    - drop a matching yaml into `deploy-approvals/<stack>/`;
    - start a background process that rewrites `$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json`;
    - or simply call AWS directly with the deploy role during preview.

    - (a) State the threat model explicitly (accidental risky diffs only).
    - (b) [design] Preview with a separate prod *preview* role (read plus state backend), and assume the deploy role only in a later job, after the stop.
    - (c) Run the classifier in a separate job with a fresh checkout. It must not trust the workspace of the job that ran the stack code.
  
  **M3 — `risk-stop/classify.py:38-55`. The type denylist lets risky changes through silently, and Pulumi and CloudFormation are covered differently.**
  - **Evidence (✅, `reasons_for` on update):** these return `[]`:
    - `aws:kms/key:Key` (inline key policy), while `AWS::KMS::Key` is flagged;
    - `aws:sqs/queue:Queue` (inline `policy`);

    - `aws:ecs/taskDefinition` (task role change);
    - `aws:s3/bucketPublicAccessBlock`.

  - **Effect:** this conflicts with ADR-0004's "an IAM change … stops". The "examples, not complete" comment does not cover how the design fails, only that the list is short.
  - **Fix:**
    - Fail closed on resource types: anything not on a known-safe allowlist is risky, OR flag changes to property names such as `policy`, `assumeRolePolicy`, `role`, `*SecurityGroup*`, `vpcConfig`, `authorizationType`.
    - Make the two type lists match each other.
    - Add a test per category for both Pulumi and CloudFormation.
  
  **M4 — `classify.py:86-113`. Approval binding is weak.**
  - **Problem:** `stopped_commit` is parsed but never checked, and approvals never expire. As a result:
    - (a) An approval can be replayed: any later deploy with the same diff (e.g. after a revert and re-apply, or after drift) is approved by an old file.
    - (b) A single PR can contain both the risky change and an approval file with a predicted hash. The hash covers type, name, op and a digest of old/new inputs, and all of these can be derived from code.   - **Fix:**
    - Require `stopped_commit` to be a strict ancestor of `HEAD`, and the approval file to be added in a commit after it (`git log --diff-filter=A`).
    - Make approvals one-shot, e.g. bound to the stopped commit and HEAD distance, or expiring.
    - Test both cases.
  
  **M5 — `risk-stop/adapters.py:60-72`. The Serverless hash is probably never stable.**
  - **Problem:** ⚠️ From memory of Serverless source, not checked: the packaged template's `AWS::Lambda::Function` `Code.S3Key` contains a timestamped artifact directory (`serverless/<svc>/<stage>/<epoch>-<iso>/`).   - **README status:** E7 only has the generic note "hash stability not proven".
  - **Fix:** name this concrete cause as an open item, and digest only properties that matter for the risk, leaving out volatile ones such as `Code.S3Key` and version logical IDs. Or compare the structured risky subset only, which is ADR-0004's own fallback.
  
  ### LOW
  
  **L1 — `test_workflow_policy.py:109-117`. The forbidden-flag check only looks for long flag forms.**
  - **Evidence:** `pulumi up -f -y` passes the tests (✅ mutation). `-f` = `--skip-preview` and `-t` = `--target` (📖 pulumi/docs `content/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_up.md`). `--exclude` is not checked either.
  - **Fix:** tokenise the command and use a flag allowlist.
  
  **L2 — README E3 and `deploy-prod.yml:6`: "never cancelled" claims too much.**
  - **Evidence:** the GitHub docs (📖 `data/reusables/actions/actions-group-concurrency.md`) say: "any existing pending job … will be canceled". They also say FIFO order "is not guaranteed".
  - **Effect:** intermediate merged commits get no deploy run of their own, which affects the change record that is linked by run ID.
  - **Fix:** say this in the README, and consider `queue: max` (documented for github.com), which cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`.
  
  **L3 — `deploy-prod.yml:96-120`. Undocumented gap between the risk-stop preview and `pulumi up`.**
  - **Problem:** `pulumi up` previews again, and drift or an out-of-band change (JIT, drift role) between the two previews is not seen by the stop.
  - **Fix:** `pulumi preview --save-plan` + `pulumi up --plan` would close this, but `--plan` is marked "[EXPERIMENTAL]" (📖 same pulumi_up.md). Add it to "Does not prove".
  
  **L4 — `deploy-prod.yml:54-90`. Order of steps and where prod values live.**
  - `npm ci` runs after the prod credentials are configured. Install first, or use `--ignore-scripts` where possible.
  - Prod values (`PROD_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`, `PULUMI_BACKEND_URL`) are repository variables. They could be environment variables of `production` instead.
  
  **L5 — `ruleset-main.json:23`. `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes: true` is not in the framework and is not marked [design].**
  - Per R3.3.2 it is Copilot-only. Turned on, it can make a third person necessary, which goes against OD2.
  - **Fix:** drop it, or mark it [design] with the reason.
  
  **L6 — `classify.py:57,68`. `CHURN` is dead code.**
  - `STATEFUL` never matches `AWS::Lambda::Version`. With the CHURN condition removed, all tests still pass (✅ mutation).
  - The test `test_lambda_version_churn_is_not_a_stateful_delete` proves nothing, so README finding 3 is not shown by code.
  
  **L7 — README Rule 1 markers and wording.**
  - Findings 3–5, "actionlint 1.7.12 (latest, March 2026)" and "App ID 15368" have no ✅ or 📖 link.
  - The summary is described as "posted", but it is only uploaded as an artifact. The framework says it "posts the filtered preview"; at least write it to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.
  
  **L8 — Untracked `__pycache__/*.pyc` files in `examples/risk-stop` and `examples/tests`.**
  - There is no `.gitignore`, so `git add examples/` would commit them. Add one, or use `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` in `validate.sh`.
  
  ### What is consistent with the framework
  - E1 has every rule that the plan requires.
  - E3b's environment and branch-policy bodies are correct, with no reviewers.
  - `secrets.md` lists names only.
  - The workflows have per-job permissions, SHA-pinned actions, no forbidden triggers, no ref input, and OIDC only where needed.
  - The README's "does not prove" columns are honest, apart from the gaps listed above.
  
  **Verdict:** this needs fixes before it is presented. H1 and M1–M5 must be fixed or documented; the rest of the structure is sound and matches the framework.

  **Baseline.** I ran `examples/validate.sh` with the given actionlint and zizmor (✅). jq, yamllint, actionlint and zizmor gave no findings, the 43 unit tests passed, and the result was "all executed checks passed". I checked the `$/.github/workflows/<file>` syntax against the GitHub docs source (📖 github/docs `data/reusables/actions/reusable-workflow-calling-syntax.md`, which calls it "the recommended syntax"), so README finding 4 is correct. I ran the mutation tests on a copy in `.../scratchpad/review/ex`. I found no secrets, account IDs, ARNs or emails in examples/; everything uses placeholders. Nothing touches live systems.
  
  ### HIGH
  
  **H1 — `github/CODEOWNERS:32-34` against `github/workflows/deploy-on-main.yml:24-32`. The approvals folder for stack `claims-api` has no owner.**
  - **Problem:** `deploy-on-main` deploys a `claims-api` stack, so the classifier reads `deploy-approvals/claims-api/`. CODEOWNERS has no line for that folder.
  - **Effect:** any writer can approve a risk-stop approval for that stack. That breaks OD8 and ADR-0004 ("owned by the stack's owners and the on-call group").
  - **Evidence:** the resolver from `tests/test_codeowners.py` returns `None` for `deploy-approvals/claims-api/abc.yaml`, for `deploy-approvals/<new-stack>/…`, and also for root `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `infra/pulumi/shared/…`. Unowned files need only "1 approval by any writer", not a code owner. No test catches this because `RISK_STOP_SAMPLES` is hand-written.
  - **Fix:**
    - Add `/deploy-approvals/claims-api/`.
    - Add a fail-safe catch-all at the top, e.g. `/deploy-approvals/ @l3-owners` and/or `* @oncall-approvers <default team>`.
    - Add a test that takes every `stack:` and `workdir:` from `deploy-on-main.yml` and asserts that both `deploy-approvals/<stack>/x.yaml` and `<workdir>/x` resolve to domain team + on-call.
  
  ### MEDIUM
  
  **M1 — `tests/test_workflow_policy.py:119-124`. The tests do not prove that the risk stop actually blocks the apply.**
  - **Problem:** the only check is the order of the step names.
  - **Evidence:** I made each of these changes alone, and each passed all 43 tests, actionlint and zizmor:
    - `continue-on-error: true` on the "Risk stop" step;
    - `python3 tools/risk-stop/classify.py || true; …`;
    - `if: always() && inputs.tool == 'pulumi'` on the Apply step.
  
    This is the core of the [design] control, and README E3 says "preview → risk stop → apply" is checked.
  - **Fix:** assert three things:
    - The Risk stop step has no `continue-on-error` or `if:`.
    - Its `run` starts with the classifier call and has no `||` or `;` after it.
    - Every Apply step's `if` is exactly `inputs.tool == '<tool>'`, with no `always()`, `failure()` or `!cancelled()`.
  
  **M2 — `github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml:59-101`. Stack code can tamper with the risk stop.**
  - **Problem:** in the same job, `npm ci`, the Pulumi program (run by `preview`) and `serverless package` plugins all run **with the prod deploy role already assumed**. They also run before the classifier, with write access to the workspace.
  - **What that code can do:**
    - overwrite `tools/risk-stop/classify.py`;
    - drop a matching yaml into `deploy-approvals/<stack>/`;
    - start a background process that rewrites `$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json`;
    - or simply call AWS directly with the deploy role during preview.
  - **Effect:** README finding 1 (make the classifier an L3 path) does not hold inside this job. So the risk stop only protects against honest mistakes, not against malicious or prompt-injected code that has been approved. The README and the framework do not say this.
  - **Fix:**
    - (a) State the threat model explicitly (accidental risky diffs only).
    - (b) [design] Preview with a separate prod *preview* role (read plus state backend), and assume the deploy role only in a later job, after the stop.
    - (c) Run the classifier in a separate job with a fresh checkout. It must not trust the workspace of the job that ran the stack code.
  
  **M3 — `risk-stop/classify.py:38-55`. The type denylist lets risky changes through silently, and Pulumi and CloudFormation are covered differently.**
  - **Evidence (✅, `reasons_for` on update):** these return `[]`:
    - `aws:kms/key:Key` (inline key policy), while `AWS::KMS::Key` is flagged;
    - `aws:sqs/queue:Queue` (inline `policy`);
    - `aws:sns/topicPolicy`, `AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy`;
    - `AWS::ApiGateway::*` and `AWS::ApiGatewayV2::*`. Serverless http events use these, while Pulumi `aws:apigateway/` is flagged.
    - `aws:lambda/functionUrl`, `AWS::Lambda::Url`;
    - `aws:ecs/taskDefinition` (task role change);
    - `aws:s3/bucketPublicAccessBlock`.
  
    On delete, `aws:cloudwatch/logGroup` and `AWS::Logs::LogGroup` (audit logs) and `aws:ec2/instance` also return `[]`.
  - **Effect:** this conflicts with ADR-0004's "an IAM change … stops". The "examples, not complete" comment does not cover how the design fails, only that the list is short.
  - **Fix:**
    - Fail closed on resource types: anything not on a known-safe allowlist is risky, OR flag changes to property names such as `policy`, `assumeRolePolicy`, `role`, `*SecurityGroup*`, `vpcConfig`, `authorizationType`.
    - Make the two type lists match each other.
    - Add a test per category for both Pulumi and CloudFormation.
  
  **M4 — `classify.py:86-113`. Approval binding is weak.**
  - **Problem:** `stopped_commit` is parsed but never checked, and approvals never expire. As a result:
    - (a) An approval can be replayed: any later deploy with the same diff (e.g. after a revert and re-apply, or after drift) is approved by an old file.
    - (b) A single PR can contain both the risky change and an approval file with a predicted hash. The hash covers type, name, op and a digest of old/new inputs, and all of these can be derived from code. That skips the "second look at the prod diff" that the framework (layer 3) and ADR-0004 describe.
  - **Fix:**
    - Require `stopped_commit` to be a strict ancestor of `HEAD`, and the approval file to be added in a commit after it (`git log --diff-filter=A`).
    - Make approvals one-shot, e.g. bound to the stopped commit and HEAD distance, or expiring.
    - Test both cases.
  
  **M5 — `risk-stop/adapters.py:60-72`. The Serverless hash is probably never stable.**
  - **Problem:** ⚠️ From memory of Serverless source, not checked: the packaged template's `AWS::Lambda::Function` `Code.S3Key` contains a timestamped artifact directory (`serverless/<svc>/<stage>/<epoch>-<iso>/`). If that is right, every `package` changes the digest, so a stopped Serverless stack can never be approved and stops forever.
  - **README status:** E7 only has the generic note "hash stability not proven".
  - **Fix:** name this concrete cause as an open item, and digest only properties that matter for the risk, leaving out volatile ones such as `Code.S3Key` and version logical IDs. Or compare the structured risky subset only, which is ADR-0004's own fallback.
  
  ### LOW
  
  **L1 — `test_workflow_policy.py:109-117`. The forbidden-flag check only looks for long flag forms.**
  - **Evidence:** `pulumi up -f -y` passes the tests (✅ mutation). `-f` = `--skip-preview` and `-t` = `--target` (📖 pulumi/docs `content/docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_up.md`). `--exclude` is not checked either.
  - **Fix:** tokenise the command and use a flag allowlist.
  
  **L2 — README E3 and `deploy-prod.yml:6`: "never cancelled" claims too much.**
  - **Evidence:** the GitHub docs (📖 `data/reusables/actions/actions-group-concurrency.md`) say: "any existing pending job … will be canceled". They also say FIFO order "is not guaranteed".
  - **Effect:** intermediate merged commits get no deploy run of their own, which affects the change record that is linked by run ID.
  - **Fix:** say this in the README, and consider `queue: max` (documented for github.com), which cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`.
  
  **L3 — `deploy-prod.yml:96-120`. Undocumented gap between the risk-stop preview and `pulumi up`.**
  - **Problem:** `pulumi up` previews again, and drift or an out-of-band change (JIT, drift role) between the two previews is not seen by the stop.
  - **Fix:** `pulumi preview --save-plan` + `pulumi up --plan` would close this, but `--plan` is marked "[EXPERIMENTAL]" (📖 same pulumi_up.md). Add it to "Does not prove".
  
  **L4 — `deploy-prod.yml:54-90`. Order of steps and where prod values live.**
  - `npm ci` runs after the prod credentials are configured. Install first, or use `--ignore-scripts` where possible.
  - Prod values (`PROD_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN`, `PULUMI_BACKEND_URL`) are repository variables. They could be environment variables of `production` instead.
  
  **L5 — `ruleset-main.json:23`. `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes: true` is not in the framework and is not marked [design].**
  - Per R3.3.2 it is Copilot-only. Turned on, it can make a third person necessary, which goes against OD2.
  - **Fix:** drop it, or mark it [design] with the reason.
  
  **L6 — `classify.py:57,68`. `CHURN` is dead code.**
  - `STATEFUL` never matches `AWS::Lambda::Version`. With the CHURN condition removed, all tests still pass (✅ mutation).
  - The test `test_lambda_version_churn_is_not_a_stateful_delete` proves nothing, so README finding 3 is not shown by code.
  
  **L7 — README Rule 1 markers and wording.**
  - Findings 3–5, "actionlint 1.7.12 (latest, March 2026)" and "App ID 15368" have no ✅ or 📖 link.
  - The summary is described as "posted", but it is only uploaded as an artifact. The framework says it "posts the filtered preview"; at least write it to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.
  
  **L8 — Untracked `__pycache__/*.pyc` files in `examples/risk-stop` and `examples/tests`.**
  - There is no `.gitignore`, so `git add examples/` would commit them. Add one, or use `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` in `validate.sh`.
  
  ### What is consistent with the framework
  - E1 has every rule that the plan requires.
  - E3b's environment and branch-policy bodies are correct, with no reviewers.
  - `secrets.md` lists names only.
  - The workflows have per-job permissions, SHA-pinned actions, no forbidden triggers, no ref input, and OIDC only where needed.
  - The README's "does not prove" columns are honest, apart from the gaps listed above.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Risk stop for production deploys (framework layer 3, ADR-0004) [design].

Reads a prod preview, decides whether it contains a risky change, and either lets the
deploy continue or stops it until an owner of the stack approves this exact preview.

  exit 0  no risky change, or a valid approval matches this preview's hash
  exit 3  risky change and no valid approval: STOP, nothing is applied
  exit 2  the preview could not be read: STOP (fail closed)

What it guards against: risky prod diffs that the PR approver did not see, because on GitHub
Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply (framework §1). It is NOT a boundary against
malicious code that was approved: the stack's own code runs with the deploy role during the
preview and during `pulumi up` (see examples/README.md, "Limits of the risk stop").

Risky (whatever the change level):
  - replace or delete of a stateful resource (data, keys, logs);
  - any change to an IAM, resource-policy or network resource type;
  - a change to a property whose NAME looks like access or network control (policy, role,
    security group, VPC, public access, authorization, principal, KMS key), on any type;
  - an operation the classifier does not know.
Advisory policy findings join in phase 2 (not implemented here).

Approval (framework layer 3; OD8, OD13): the original author opens a PR that adds
deploy-approvals/<stack>/<stopped-commit>.yaml with `preview_hash`; CODEOWNERS makes an owner of
the stack (or the on-call group) approve it. An approval counts only if, in git history:
  1. `stopped_commit` is a strict ancestor of HEAD;
  2. the file was added after `stopped_commit`, by a commit that changes nothing outside
     deploy-approvals/<stack>/ (so a PR cannot carry its own risky change and its approval);
  3. that commit is at most MAX_AGE_DAYS older than HEAD (no replay of old approvals).
The deploy previews again on the new HEAD and continues only if the hash is the same, so any
change merged in between stops it again (Options §1).

The hash covers type, name, operation and a digest of the changed values, leaving out values
that change on every build (adapters.py). The summary shows type, name, operation and changed
property NAMES only: no values, outputs or secrets.

Normalized input (produced by adapters.py from the tool's own JSON):
  {"changes": [{"type": "aws:iam/role:Role", "name": "deployer", "op": "update",
                "changed_keys": ["assumeRolePolicy"], "detail_digest": "<sha256>"}]}
  op: create | update | replace | delete | same | <anything else = unknown>
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

import adapters

MAX_AGE_DAYS = 7  # [design]

# Each category lists the Pulumi AWS type prefix and the matching CloudFormation type, side by
# side, so the two tools are covered alike. Examples, not complete [design]; the property-name
# rule below is the safety net for types that are missing here.
STATEFUL_TYPES = [
    ("aws:rds/", "AWS::RDS::"),
    ("aws:s3/bucket:", "AWS::S3::Bucket"),
    ("aws:s3/bucketV2:", "AWS::S3::Bucket"),
    ("aws:dynamodb/table", "AWS::DynamoDB::Table"),
    ("aws:efs/", "AWS::EFS::"),
    ("aws:kms/key:", "AWS::KMS::Key"),
    ("aws:sqs/queue:", "AWS::SQS::Queue"),
    ("aws:sns/topic:", "AWS::SNS::Topic"),
    ("aws:elasticache/", "AWS::ElastiCache::"),
    ("aws:secretsmanager/secret:", "AWS::SecretsManager::Secret"),
    ("aws:cloudwatch/logGroup", "AWS::Logs::LogGroup"),
    ("aws:cloudtrail/", "AWS::CloudTrail::"),
    ("aws:ec2/instance", "AWS::EC2::Instance"),
    ("aws:ebs/", "AWS::EC2::Volume"),
    ("aws:opensearch/", "AWS::OpenSearchService::"),
    ("aws:backup/", "AWS::Backup::"),
]
ACCESS_TYPES = [
    ("aws:iam/", "AWS::IAM::"),
    ("aws:organizations/", "AWS::Organizations::"),
    ("aws:s3/bucketPolicy", "AWS::S3::BucketPolicy"),
    ("aws:s3/bucketPublicAccessBlock", "AWS::S3::BucketPublicAccessBlock"),
    ("aws:sqs/queuePolicy", "AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy"),
    ("aws:sns/topicPolicy", "AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy"),
    ("aws:lambda/permission", "AWS::Lambda::Permission"),
    ("aws:lambda/functionUrl", "AWS::Lambda::Url"),
    ("aws:kms/keyPolicy", "AWS::KMS::Key"),
    ("aws:kms/grant", "AWS::KMS::Grant"),
    ("aws:secretsmanager/secretPolicy", "AWS::SecretsManager::ResourcePolicy"),
    ("aws:apigateway/", "AWS::ApiGateway::"),
    ("aws:apigatewayv2/", "AWS::ApiGatewayV2::"),
    ("aws:cognito/", "AWS::Cognito::"),
]
NETWORK_TYPES = [
    ("aws:ec2/securityGroup", "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup"),
    ("aws:vpc/", "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup"),
    ("aws:ec2/vpc", "AWS::EC2::VPC"),
    ("aws:ec2/subnet", "AWS::EC2::Subnet"),
    ("aws:ec2/routeTable", "AWS::EC2::RouteTable"),
    ("aws:ec2/route:", "AWS::EC2::Route"),
    ("aws:ec2/internetGateway", "AWS::EC2::InternetGateway"),
    ("aws:ec2/natGateway", "AWS::EC2::NatGateway"),
    ("aws:ec2/networkAcl", "AWS::EC2::NetworkAcl"),
    ("aws:ec2/vpcEndpoint", "AWS::EC2::VPCEndpoint"),
    ("aws:ec2/vpcPeeringConnection", "AWS::EC2::VPCPeeringConnection"),
    ("aws:ec2/eip", "AWS::EC2::EIP"),
    ("aws:lb/", "AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::"),
    ("aws:alb/", "AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::"),
    ("aws:cloudfront/", "AWS::CloudFront::"),
    ("aws:route53/", "AWS::Route53::"),
]
RISKY_KEY = re.compile(
    r"polic|assumerole|role(arn)?$|^role|securitygroup|vpcconfig|subnet|publicaccess|"
    r"authoriz|principal|kmskey|grant|acl$|cors|trust",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
KNOWN_OPS = {"create", "update", "replace", "delete", "same"}


def _matches(rtype, table):
    return any(rtype.startswith(p) or rtype.startswith(c) for p, c in table)


def reasons_for(change):
    t, op = change["type"], change["op"]
    if op == "same":
        return []
    if op not in KNOWN_OPS:
        return [f"unknown operation '{op}'"]
    out = []
    if op in ("replace", "delete") and _matches(t, STATEFUL_TYPES):
        out.append(f"{op} of a stateful resource")
    if _matches(t, ACCESS_TYPES):
        out.append("IAM or resource-policy change")
    if _matches(t, NETWORK_TYPES):
        out.append("network change")
    keys = sorted(k for k in change.get("changed_keys", []) if RISKY_KEY.search(k))
    if keys and op in ("update", "replace"):
        out.append("access or network property changed: " + ", ".join(keys))
    return out


def preview_hash(changes):
    material = sorted(
        (c["type"], c["name"], c["op"], c.get("detail_digest", ""))
        for c in changes
        if c["op"] != "same" and not c.get("volatile")
    )
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(material).encode()).hexdigest()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- approvals

def _git(repo, *args):
    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", repo, *args], capture_output=True, text=True)


def _is_ancestor(repo, a, b):
    return _git(repo, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", a, b).returncode == 0


def _commit_time(repo, rev):
    out = _git(repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%ct", rev).stdout.strip()
    return datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(int(out), datetime.timezone.utc)


def _parse_yaml_flat(path):
    fields = {}
    with open(path) as f:
        for line in f:
            m = re.match(r"^([a-z_]+)\s*:\s*\"?([^\"#]*?)\"?\s*(#.*)?$", line)
            if m:
                fields[m.group(1)] = m.group(2).strip()
    return fields


def check_approval(repo, approvals_dir, name):
    """Return (preview_hash, None) if the approval file is valid, else (None, reason)."""
    rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(approvals_dir, name), repo)
    fields = _parse_yaml_flat(os.path.join(repo, rel))
    h, stopped = fields.get("preview_hash", ""), fields.get("stopped_commit", "")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", h):
        return None, "no valid preview_hash"
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", stopped):
        return None, "no valid stopped_commit"
    head = _git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout.strip()

            m = re.match(r"^([a-z_]+)\s*:\s*\"?([^\"#]*?)\"?\s*(#.*)?$", line)
            if m:
                fields[m.group(1)] = m.group(2).strip()
    return fields


def check_approval(repo, approvals_dir, name):
    """Return (preview_hash, None) if the approval file is valid, else (None, reason)."""
    rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(approvals_dir, name), repo)
    fields = _parse_yaml_flat(os.path.join(repo, rel))
    h, stopped = fields.get("preview_hash", ""), fields.get("stopped_commit", "")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", h):
        return None, "no valid preview_hash"
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", stopped):
        return None, "no valid stopped_commit"
    head = _git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD").stdout.strip()
    if stopped == head or not _is_ancestor(repo, stopped, head):
        return None, "stopped_commit is not a strict ancestor of HEAD"
    added = _git(repo, "log", "--diff-filter=A", "--format=%H", "-n", "1", "--", rel).stdout.strip()
    if not added:
        return None, "file is not in git history"
    if added == stopped or not _is_ancestor(repo, stopped, added):
        return None, "file was not added after stopped_commit"
    touched = _git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", f"{added}^1", added).stdout.split()
    prefix = os.path.relpath(approvals_dir, repo).rstrip("/") + "/"
    if any(not p.startswith(prefix) for p in touched):
        return None, "the commit that added it also changes files outside " + prefix
    age = _commit_time(repo, head) - _commit_time(repo, added)
    if age > datetime.timedelta(days=MAX_AGE_DAYS):
        return None, f"older than {MAX_AGE_DAYS} days"
    return h, None


def read_approvals(repo, approvals_dir):
    """Return ({preview_hash: file}, [(file, reason) for rejected files])."""
    valid, rejected = {}, []
    if not os.path.isdir(approvals_dir):
        return valid, rejected
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(approvals_dir)):
        if name.endswith((".yaml", ".yml")):
            h, why = check_approval(repo, approvals_dir, name)
            if h:
                valid[h] = name
            else:
                rejected.append((name, why))
    return valid, rejected


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- decision

def decide(normalized, approvals):
    changes = normalized["changes"]
    risky = [(c, r) for c in changes for r in [reasons_for(c)] if r]
    h = preview_hash(changes)
    if not risky:
        return 0, h, risky, None
    if h in approvals:
        return 0, h, risky, approvals[h]
    return 3, h, risky, None


def summary_text(code, h, risky, approved_by_file, rejected=()):
    lines = ["# Risk stop", "", f"Preview hash: `{h}`", ""]
    if not risky:
        lines.append("No risky change. Deploy continues.")
    elif code == 0:
        lines.append(f"Risky changes approved by `{approved_by_file}` (hash matches). Deploy continues.")
    else:
        lines += [
            "**Deploy stopped.** Risky changes need an approval from an owner of this stack:",
            "open a PR that adds only `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<this commit>.yaml` with the hash above.",
        ]
    if risky:
        lines += ["", "| Type | Name | Operation | Why |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
        for c, r in risky:
            lines.append(f"| `{c['type']}` | `{c['name']}` | {c['op']} | {'; '.join(r)} |")
    if rejected:
        lines += ["", "Approval files not accepted:"]
        lines += [f"- `{n}`: {why}" for n, why in rejected]
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    p.add_argument("--tool", required=True, choices=["pulumi", "serverless", "normalized"])
    p.add_argument("--preview", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--approvals", required=True, help="deploy-approvals/<stack> directory")
    p.add_argument("--repo", default=".", help="git checkout with full history")
    p.add_argument("--summary", help="write the markdown summary here as well")
    a = p.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        with open(a.preview) as f:
            raw = json.load(f)
        normalized = adapters.ADAPTERS[a.tool](raw)
    except Exception as e:  # fail closed
        print(f"risk-stop: cannot read preview ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); stopping", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    approvals, rejected = read_approvals(a.repo, a.approvals)
    code, h, risky, approved = decide(normalized, approvals)
    text = summary_text(code, h, risky, approved, rejected)
    print(text)
    for path in filter(None, [a.summary, os.environ.get("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY")]):
        with open(path, "a") as f:
            f.write(text)
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Risk stop for production deploys (framework layer 3, ADR-0004) [design].

Reads a prod preview, decides whether it contains a risky change, and either lets the
deploy continue or stops it until an owner of the stack approves this exact preview.

  exit 0  no risky change, or an approval file matches this preview's hash
  exit 3  risky change and no matching approval: STOP, nothing is applied
  exit 2  the preview could not be read: STOP (fail closed)

Risky (whatever the change level): replace or delete of a stateful resource; any change
to IAM or resource policies; any network or security-group change; an operation the
classifier does not know. Advisory policy findings join in phase 2 (not implemented here).

Approval: the original author opens a PR adding deploy-approvals/<stack>/<commit>.yaml with
`preview_hash`; CODEOWNERS makes the stack's owners (or the on-call group) approve it. Merging
it triggers a new deploy, which previews again: it continues only if the hash is the same, so
any change merged in between stops it again (Options §1).

The hash covers type, name, operation and a digest of the changed values. The summary that
is posted shows type, name and operation only: no property values, outputs or secrets.

Input: the normalized format below, produced by adapters.py from the tool's own JSON.
  {"changes": [{"type": "aws:iam/role:Role", "name": "deployer", "op": "update",
                "detail_digest": "<sha256 of the changed values>"}]}
  op: create | update | replace | delete | same | <anything else = unknown>
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import sys

import adapters

# Pulumi type tokens and CloudFormation types. Lists are examples, not complete [design].
STATEFUL = re.compile(
    r"^(aws:rds/|aws:s3/bucket(V2)?:|aws:dynamodb/table|aws:efs/|aws:kms/key|aws:sqs/queue:"
    r"|aws:elasticache/|aws:secretsmanager/secret:"
    r"|AWS::RDS::|AWS::S3::Bucket$|AWS::DynamoDB::Table|AWS::EFS::|AWS::KMS::Key"
    r"|AWS::SQS::Queue$|AWS::ElastiCache::|AWS::SecretsManager::Secret$)"
)
IAM = re.compile(
    r"^(aws:iam/|aws:organizations/policy|aws:s3/bucketPolicy|aws:sqs/queuePolicy"
    r"|aws:lambda/permission|aws:kms/keyPolicy|aws:secretsmanager/secretPolicy"
    r"|AWS::IAM::|AWS::Organizations::Policy|AWS::S3::BucketPolicy|AWS::SQS::QueuePolicy"
    r"|AWS::Lambda::Permission|AWS::KMS::Key$)"
)
NETWORK = re.compile(
    r"^(aws:ec2/(securityGroup|vpc|subnet|routeTable|route:|internetGateway|natGateway"
    r"|networkAcl|vpcEndpoint|vpcPeering|eip)|aws:vpc/|aws:lb/|aws:alb/|aws:apigateway/"
    r"|AWS::EC2::(SecurityGroup|VPC|Subnet|RouteTable|Route$|InternetGateway|NatGateway"
    r"|NetworkAcl|VPCEndpoint|VPCPeering|EIP)|AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::)"
)
# Replaced on every code change by Serverless; not data, so not "stateful".
CHURN = re.compile(r"^AWS::Lambda::Version$")
KNOWN_OPS = {"create", "update", "replace", "delete", "same"}


def reasons_for(change):
    t, op = change["type"], change["op"]
    if op == "same":
        return []
    if op not in KNOWN_OPS:
        return [f"unknown operation '{op}'"]
    out = []
    if op in ("replace", "delete") and STATEFUL.search(t) and not CHURN.search(t):
        out.append(f"{op} of a stateful resource")
    if IAM.search(t):
        out.append("IAM or resource-policy change")
    if NETWORK.search(t):
        out.append("network change")
    return out


def preview_hash(changes):
    material = sorted(
        (c["type"], c["name"], c["op"], c.get("detail_digest", ""))
        for c in changes
        if c["op"] != "same"
    )
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(material).encode()).hexdigest()


def read_approvals(directory):
    """Return {preview_hash: file} from deploy-approvals/<stack>/*.yaml (flat `key: value`)."""
    found = {}
    if not os.path.isdir(directory):
        return found
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(directory)):
        if not name.endswith((".yaml", ".yml")):
            continue
        fields = {}
        with open(os.path.join(directory, name)) as f:
            for line in f:
                m = re.match(r"^\s*([a-z_]+)\s*:\s*\"?([^\"#]*?)\"?\s*(#.*)?$", line)
                if m:
                    fields[m.group(1)] = m.group(2).strip()
        if re.fullmatch(r"sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}", fields.get("preview_hash", "")):
            found[fields["preview_hash"]] = name
    return found


def decide(normalized, approvals):
    changes = normalized["changes"]
    risky = [(c, r) for c in changes for r in [reasons_for(c)] if r]
    h = preview_hash(changes)
    if not risky:
        return 0, h, risky, None
    if h in approvals:
        return 0, h, risky, approvals[h]
    return 3, h, risky, None


def summary_text(code, h, risky, approved_by_file):
    lines = ["# Risk stop", "", f"Preview hash: `{h}`", ""]
    if not risky:
        lines.append("No risky change. Deploy continues.")
    elif code == 0:
        lines.append(f"Risky changes approved by `{approved_by_file}` (hash matches). Deploy continues.")
    else:
        lines += [
            "**Deploy stopped.** Risky changes need an approval from an owner of this stack:",
            "open a PR adding `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<commit>.yaml` with the hash above.",
        ]
    if risky:
        lines += ["", "| Type | Name | Operation | Why |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
        for c, r in risky:
            lines.append(f"| `{c['type']}` | `{c['name']}` | {c['op']} | {'; '.join(r)} |")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    p.add_argument("--tool", required=True, choices=["pulumi", "serverless", "normalized"])
    p.add_argument("--preview", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--approvals", required=True, help="deploy-approvals/<stack> directory")
    p.add_argument("--summary", help="write the markdown summary here as well")
    a = p.parse_args(argv)
    try:
        with open(a.preview) as f:
            raw = json.load(f)
        normalized = adapters.ADAPTERS[a.tool](raw)
    except Exception as e:  # fail closed
        print(f"risk-stop: cannot read preview ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); stopping", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    code, h, risky, approved = decide(normalized, read_approvals(a.approvals))
    text = summary_text(code, h, risky, approved)
    print(text)
    if a.summary:
        with open(a.summary, "w") as f:
            f.write(text)
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""E7: risk stop classifier (examples/risk-stop/).

Proves the [design] logic: what stops a deploy (per category, for Pulumi and CloudFormation
types alike), that an approval counts only for the exact preview and only with the git
history the framework's flow produces, and that the summary carries no property values.

Approval tests build a throwaway git repository, because the approval rules are about history:
the stopped commit must be an ancestor of HEAD, the approval must be added later by a commit
that touches only deploy-approvals/<stack>/, and it must be recent.

Does NOT prove: the real JSON shape of `pulumi preview --json` / `serverless diff --json`
(adapters are ⚠️ assumptions, fixtures are hand-written), nor that a real preview gives the
same hash twice for unchanged code (⚠️ Options §8).
"""
import io
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stderr, redirect_stdout

HERE = os.path.dirname(__file__)
RS = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "risk-stop")
sys.path.insert(0, RS)
import adapters  # noqa: E402
import classify  # noqa: E402


def fixture(name):
    return os.path.join(RS, "fixtures", name)


def load(name):
    with open(fixture(name)) as f:
        return json.load(f)


def run(tool, preview, approvals, repo="."):
    out = io.StringIO()
    env_summary = os.environ.pop("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY", None)
    try:
        with redirect_stdout(out), redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
            code = classify.main(["--tool", tool, "--preview", preview,
                                  "--approvals", approvals, "--repo", repo])
    finally:
        if env_summary is not None:
            os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"] = env_summary
    return code, out.getvalue()


def risky(change):
    return bool(classify.reasons_for(change))


class Repo:
    """A throwaway git repository with a fixed identity (no real person)."""

    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = path
        self.git("init", "-q", "-b", "main")
        self.date = 1_800_000_000  # fixed clock, advanced per commit

    def git(self, *args, env=None):
        full_env = dict(os.environ, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=os.devnull,
                        GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="test", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="test@example.invalid",
                        GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="test", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="test@example.invalid")
        full_env.update(env or {})
        r = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", self.path, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, env=full_env)
        if r.returncode:
            raise RuntimeError(r.stderr)
        return r.stdout.strip()

    def commit(self, files, msg, days_later=0):
        for rel, content in files.items():
            p = os.path.join(self.path, rel)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)
            with open(p, "w") as f:
                f.write(content)
        self.git("add", "-A")
        self.date += 60 + days_later * 86400
        stamp = f"@{self.date} +0000"
        self.git("commit", "-q", "-m", msg, env={"GIT_AUTHOR_DATE": stamp, "GIT_COMMITTER_DATE": stamp})
        return self.git("rev-parse", "HEAD")


def approval_yaml(stopped, h):
    return f"stack: claims-data\nstopped_commit: {stopped}\npreview_hash: {h}\n"


class ClassificationTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_benign_change_continues(self):
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", fixture("normalized-benign.json"), "/nonexistent")[0], 0)

    def test_iam_change_stops(self):
        code, out = run("normalized", fixture("normalized-iam.json"), "/nonexistent")
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
        self.assertIn("IAM", out)

    def test_stateful_replace_stops(self):
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", fixture("normalized-stateful-delete.json"), "/nonexistent")[0], 3)

    def test_categories_for_both_tools(self):
        cases = [
            # (type, op, changed_keys) -> must be risky
            ("aws:iam/role:Role", "update", []), ("AWS::IAM::Role", "update", []),
            ("aws:ec2/securityGroup:SecurityGroup", "update", []), ("AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup", "update", []),
            ("aws:apigateway/method:Method", "update", []), ("AWS::ApiGateway::Method", "update", []),
            ("aws:apigatewayv2/route:Route", "update", []), ("AWS::ApiGatewayV2::Route", "update", []),
            ("aws:lambda/functionUrl:FunctionUrl", "create", []), ("AWS::Lambda::Url", "create", []),
            ("aws:sns/topicPolicy:TopicPolicy", "update", []), ("AWS::SNS::TopicPolicy", "update", []),
            ("aws:s3/bucketPublicAccessBlock:BucketPublicAccessBlock", "update", []),
            ("AWS::S3::BucketPublicAccessBlock", "update", []),
            ("aws:cloudwatch/logGroup:LogGroup", "delete", []), ("AWS::Logs::LogGroup", "delete", []),
            ("aws:ec2/instance:Instance", "delete", []), ("AWS::EC2::Instance", "delete", []),
            ("aws:rds/cluster:Cluster", "replace", []), ("AWS::RDS::DBCluster", "replace", []),
            # inline policies and roles on types that are not in any list
            ("aws:kms/key:Key", "update", ["policy"]), ("aws:sqs/queue:Queue", "update", ["policy"]),
            ("aws:ecs/taskDefinition:TaskDefinition", "update", ["taskRoleArn"]),
            ("AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition", "update", ["TaskRoleArn"]),
            ("aws:lambda/function:Function", "update", ["vpcConfig"]),
            ("AWS::Lambda::Function", "update", ["Role"]),
        ]
        for t, op, keys in cases:
            with self.subTest(type=t, op=op, keys=keys):
                self.assertTrue(risky({"type": t, "name": "x", "op": op, "changed_keys": keys}))

    def test_routine_changes_are_not_risky(self):
        for t, op, keys in [
            ("aws:lambda/function:Function", "update", ["timeout", "memorySize"]),
            ("AWS::Lambda::Function", "update", ["Timeout", "MemorySize"]),
            ("aws:ecs/service:Service", "update", ["desiredCount"]),
            ("AWS::Lambda::Version", "delete", []),  # replaced on every Serverless code change
            ("aws:sqs/queue:Queue", "update", ["visibilityTimeoutSeconds"]),
        ]:
            with self.subTest(type=t):
                self.assertFalse(risky({"type": t, "name": "x", "op": op, "changed_keys": keys}))

    def test_unknown_operation_stops(self):
        self.assertTrue(risky({"type": "aws:lambda/function:Function", "name": "f", "op": "import"}))

    def test_unreadable_preview_fails_closed(self):
        tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        try:
            p = os.path.join(tmp, "bad.json")
            with open(p, "w") as f:
                f.write("{not json")
            self.assertEqual(run("pulumi", p, "/nonexistent")[0], 2)
            with open(p, "w") as f:
                json.dump({"unexpected": []}, f)
            self.assertEqual(run("pulumi", p, "/nonexistent")[0], 2)
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(tmp)

    def test_summary_has_no_property_values(self):
        code, out = run("pulumi", fixture("pulumi-preview.json"), "/nonexistent")
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)  # S3 bucket replaced
        self.assertNotIn("PLACEHOLDER-SECRET-LIKE-VALUE", out)
        self.assertNotIn("2048", out)

    def test_serverless_adapter_iam_stops(self):
        code, out = run("serverless", fixture("serverless-diff.json"), "/nonexistent")
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
        self.assertIn("AWS::IAM::Role", out)

    def test_serverless_hash_ignores_build_volatile_values(self):
        a = {"resources": [
            {"logicalId": "FnLambdaFunction", "type": "AWS::Lambda::Function", "action": "modify",
             "properties": {"Code": {"S3Key": "serverless/svc/prod/1700000000000/fn.zip"}, "Role": "arn-a"}},
            {"logicalId": "FnLambdaVersionAAAA", "type": "AWS::Lambda::Version", "action": "add", "properties": {}}]}
        b = json.loads(json.dumps(a))
        b["resources"][0]["properties"]["Code"]["S3Key"] = "serverless/svc/prod/1700000099999/fn.zip"
        b["resources"][1]["logicalId"] = "FnLambdaVersionBBBB"
        ha = classify.preview_hash(adapters.serverless(a)["changes"])
        hb = classify.preview_hash(adapters.serverless(b)["changes"])
        self.assertEqual(ha, hb)
        b["resources"][0]["properties"]["Role"] = "arn-b"
        self.assertNotEqual(ha, classify.preview_hash(adapters.serverless(b)["changes"]))


class ApprovalTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """The approval flow of framework layer 3, against real git history."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.repo = Repo(self.tmp)
        self.preview = fixture("normalized-iam.json")
        self.h = classify.preview_hash(load("normalized-iam.json")["changes"])
        self.appr_dir = os.path.join(self.tmp, "deploy-approvals", "claims-data")
        self.base = self.repo.commit({"infra/a.ts": "v1"}, "base")
        self.stopped = self.repo.commit({"infra/a.ts": "v2 iam change"}, "risky change, deploy stopped")

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp)

    def approve(self, stopped=None, h=None, extra=None, days_later=0):
        files = {f"deploy-approvals/claims-data/{stopped or self.stopped}.yaml":
                 approval_yaml(stopped or self.stopped, h or self.h)}
        files.update(extra or {})
        return self.repo.commit(files, "approval", days_later=days_later)

    def result(self, preview=None):
        return run("normalized", preview or self.preview, self.appr_dir, repo=self.tmp)

    def test_valid_approval_continues(self):
        self.approve()
        code, out = self.result()
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertIn("approved by", out)

    def test_no_approval_stops(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.result()[0], 3)

    def test_approval_in_the_same_commit_as_the_change_is_rejected(self):
        # One PR carries both the risky change and an approval with a predicted hash,
        # naming an older commit as "stopped".
        self.approve(stopped=self.base, extra={"infra/a.ts": "v3 another iam change"})
        code, out = self.result()
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
        self.assertIn("changes files outside", out)

    def test_approval_naming_head_is_rejected(self):
        head = self.repo.git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
        self.repo.commit({f"deploy-approvals/claims-data/{head}.yaml": approval_yaml(head, self.h)}, "x")
        # stopped_commit (the previous HEAD) is an ancestor here, so name the new HEAD instead:
        new_head = self.repo.git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
        os.remove(os.path.join(self.appr_dir, f"{head}.yaml"))
        self.repo.commit({f"deploy-approvals/claims-data/{new_head}.yaml": approval_yaml(new_head, self.h)}, "y")
        latest = self.repo.git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
        with open(os.path.join(self.appr_dir, f"{new_head}.yaml"), "w") as f:
            f.write(approval_yaml(latest, self.h))  # uncommitted edit naming HEAD itself
        self.assertEqual(self.result()[0], 3)

    def test_old_approval_is_not_replayed(self):
        self.approve(days_later=0)
        self.repo.commit({"infra/b.ts": "unrelated"}, "later work", days_later=classify.MAX_AGE_DAYS + 1)
        code, out = self.result()
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
        self.assertIn("older than", out)

    def test_approval_does_not_cover_a_different_iam_change(self):
        self.approve()
        doc = load("normalized-iam.json")
        doc["changes"][1]["detail_digest"] = "policy-version-B"
        p = os.path.join(self.tmp, "b.json")
        with open(p, "w") as f:
            json.dump(doc, f)
        self.assertEqual(self.result(p)[0], 3)

    def test_change_merged_in_between_stops_again(self):
        self.approve()
        doc = load("normalized-iam.json")
        doc["changes"].append({"type": "aws:sqs/queue:Queue", "name": "x", "op": "update", "detail_digest": "z"})
        p = os.path.join(self.tmp, "later.json")
        with open(p, "w") as f:
            json.dump(doc, f)
        self.assertEqual(self.result(p)[0], 3)

    def test_uncommitted_approval_file_is_rejected(self):
        os.makedirs(self.appr_dir, exist_ok=True)
        with open(os.path.join(self.appr_dir, "dropped-at-runtime.yaml"), "w") as f:
            f.write(approval_yaml(self.stopped, self.h))
        self.assertEqual(self.result()[0], 3)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""E7: risk stop classifier (examples/risk-stop/).

Proves the [design] logic: what stops a deploy, that an approval matches only the exact
preview it was given for, and that the posted summary carries no property values.

Does NOT prove: the real JSON shape of `pulumi preview --json` / `serverless diff --json`
(adapters are ⚠️ assumptions, fixtures are hand-written), nor that a real preview gives the
same hash twice for the same code (⚠️ Options §8: unknown values, provider churn).
"""
import io
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stdout, redirect_stderr

HERE = os.path.dirname(__file__)
RS = os.path.join(HERE, "..", "risk-stop")
sys.path.insert(0, RS)
import classify  # noqa: E402


def fixture(name):
    return os.path.join(RS, "fixtures", name)


def run(tool, preview, approvals):
    out = io.StringIO()
    with redirect_stdout(out), redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
        code = classify.main(["--tool", tool, "--preview", preview, "--approvals", approvals])
    return code, out.getvalue()


class RiskStopTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.empty = os.path.join(self.tmp, "none")
        self.approved = os.path.join(RS, "deploy-approvals", "claims-data")

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.tmp)

    def write(self, name, obj):
        path = os.path.join(self.tmp, name)
        with open(path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(obj, f)
        return path

    def test_benign_change_continues(self):
        code, out = run("normalized", fixture("normalized-benign.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)

    def test_lambda_version_churn_is_not_a_stateful_delete(self):
        c = {"type": "AWS::Lambda::Version", "name": "v", "op": "delete"}
        self.assertEqual(classify.reasons_for(c), [])

    def test_iam_change_stops(self):
        code, out = run("normalized", fixture("normalized-iam.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
        self.assertIn("IAM", out)

    def test_stateful_replace_stops(self):
        code, _ = run("normalized", fixture("normalized-stateful-delete.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)

    def test_network_change_stops(self):
        p = self.write("n.json", {"changes": [
            {"type": "aws:ec2/securityGroupRule:SecurityGroupRule", "name": "ingress", "op": "create"}]})
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", p, self.empty)[0], 3)

    def test_unknown_operation_stops(self):
        p = self.write("u.json", {"changes": [{"type": "aws:lambda/function:Function", "name": "f", "op": "import"}]})
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", p, self.empty)[0], 3)

    def test_unreadable_preview_fails_closed(self):
        p = os.path.join(self.tmp, "bad.json")
        with open(p, "w") as f:
            f.write("{not json")
        self.assertEqual(run("pulumi", p, self.empty)[0], 2)
        p2 = self.write("wrong.json", {"unexpected": []})
        self.assertEqual(run("pulumi", p2, self.empty)[0], 2)

    def test_matching_approval_continues(self):
        code, out = run("normalized", fixture("normalized-iam.json"), self.approved)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out)
        self.assertIn("approved by", out)

    def test_approval_does_not_cover_a_different_iam_change(self):
        # Same resource, same operation, different policy content (A approved, B deployed).
        with open(fixture("normalized-iam.json")) as f:
            doc = json.load(f)
        doc["changes"][1]["detail_digest"] = "policy-version-B"
        p = self.write("b.json", doc)
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", p, self.approved)[0], 3)

    def test_change_merged_in_between_stops_again(self):
        with open(fixture("normalized-iam.json")) as f:
            doc = json.load(f)
        doc["changes"].append({"type": "aws:sqs/queue:Queue", "name": "x", "op": "update", "detail_digest": "z"})
        p = self.write("later.json", doc)
        self.assertEqual(run("normalized", p, self.approved)[0], 3)

    def test_summary_has_no_property_values(self):
        code, out = run("pulumi", fixture("pulumi-preview.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)  # S3 bucket replaced
        self.assertNotIn("PLACEHOLDER-SECRET-LIKE-VALUE", out)
        self.assertNotIn("2048", out)

    def test_serverless_adapter_iam_stops(self):
        code, out = run("serverless", fixture("serverless-diff.json"), self.empty)
        self.assertEqual(code, 3)
        self.assertIn("AWS::IAM::Role", out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
