### `autoMode.classifyAllShell`

Send every Bash and PowerShell command through the auto mode classifier while auto mode is active. By default, auto mode suspends only allow rules that could run arbitrary code: tool-wide and wildcard rules such as `Bash(*)`, and interpreter or shell-wrapper prefixes such as `Bash(python *)`. A command that any other allow rule matches, such as `Bash(npm test)`, skips the classifier unless it carries [per-command allowed domains](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md#per-command-allowed-domains-in-auto-mode). When it skips, a destructive argument the rule's prefix didn't anticipate can get through unseen. Setting this key suspends every shell allow rule for the session so the classifier sees every command. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.

* **Scope**: [`User or managed`](#scopes). Read wherever [`autoMode`](#automode) is read.
* **Type**: Boolean
  * `true`: while auto mode is active, Claude Code sends every Bash and PowerShell command through the classifier and suspends your shell allow rules; outside auto mode the rules still apply
  * `false`: auto mode suspends only allow rules that could run arbitrary code, such as `Bash(*)` and `Bash(python *)`; a command that any other allow rule matches skips the classifier unless it carries [per-command allowed domains](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md#per-command-allowed-domains-in-auto-mode), and every other shell command goes through it
* **Default**: `false`

```json settings.json theme={null}
{
  "autoMode": {
    "classifyAllShell": true
  }
}
```

content.content:
=== strictPluginOnlyCustomization
230:| [`strictPluginOnlyCustomization`](#strictpluginonlycustomization) | Block [skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md), [agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md), [hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md), and [MCP servers](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md) from user and project sources | Plugins and skills | Managed |
* **Default**: unset, so nothing is locked
=== forceRemoteSettingsRefresh
115:| [`forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`](#forceremotesettingsrefresh) | Block startup until [server-managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md) are freshly fetched | Enterprise and managed settings | Managed |
* **Default**: `false`
=== crossSessionInbound
68:| [`crossSessionInbound`](#crosssessioninbound) | Choose whether Claude Code delivers [messages from your other sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging.md#control-inbound-messages), shows a notice without delivering them, or refuses them | Agents, sessions, and worktrees | Any file |
Choose what this session does with [messages arriving from your other Claude Code sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cross-session-messaging.md#control-inbound-messages). When no value applies, Claude Code decides per message from the two sessions' permission-mode classes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
* **Default**: unset, so Claude Code decides per message
=== enableArtifact
96:| [`enableArtifact`](#enableartifact) | Turn the [Artifact tool](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/artifacts.md) off with a `false` in any file; no file can turn it back on | Remote, desktop, and notifications | Any file |
* **Default**: unset, so the tool follows your account's [availability](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/artifacts.md#availability)
=== disableRemoteControl
88:| [`disableRemoteControl`](#disableremotecontrol) | Turn off [Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control.md) everywhere it can start | Remote, desktop, and notifications | Any file |
* **Default**: `false`
=== cleanupPeriodDays
64:| [`cleanupPeriodDays`](#cleanupperioddays) | Choose how many days Claude Code keeps [transcripts](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage.md#data-retention) before deleting them | Privacy and telemetry | Any file |
* **Default**: `30`
=== syncClaudeAiPlugins
238:| [`syncClaudeAiPlugins`](#syncclaudeaiplugins) | Stop loading the [plugins enabled on your claude.ai account](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md#synced-plugins) and stop downloading new ones | Plugins and skills | User, local, or managed |
Turn off the download of the [plugins enabled for your claude.ai account](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md#synced-plugins). Claude Code downloads them into `~/.claude/plugins/synced/` at the start of terminal sessions where you sign in with your claude.ai account and in Cowork sessions, and loads each one as `<name>@synced`. Set `false` to stop that download and stop loading the plugins it already synced. Claude Code honors only `false`: `true` is the same as unset and doesn't turn syncing on where it's otherwise off. Requires Claude Code v2.1.273 or later.
* **Default**: unset, so sessions signed in with your claude.ai account sync your plugins
=== syncClaudeAiSkills
239:| [`syncClaudeAiSkills`](#syncclaudeaiskills) | Stop loading the [skills enabled on your claude.ai account](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md#how-synced-skills-behave) and stop downloading new ones | Plugins and skills | User, local, or managed |
* **Default**: unset, so sessions signed in with your claude.ai account sync your skills
=== skillOverrides

content.content:
### `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`

Block skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from user and project sources, so they can come only from plugins or managed settings. Combine it with [`strictKnownMarketplaces`](#strictknownmarketplaces) to control the full customization supply chain: the marketplace allowlist controls which plugins users can install.

* **Scope**: [`Managed`](#scopes)
* **Type**: `true` to lock all four kinds of customization, or an array naming the kinds to lock, from `"skills"`, `"agents"`, `"hooks"`, and `"mcp"`
* **Default**: unset, so nothing is locked

This example locks skills and hooks and leaves agents and MCP servers unlocked:

```json managed-settings.json theme={null}
{
  "strictPluginOnlyCustomization": ["skills", "hooks"]
}
```

If you lock any surface, Claude Code also stops loading [skills-directory plugins](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/loading.md#skills-directory-plugins-blocked-by-managed-settings), the plugin folders that users keep under `~/.claude/skills/` or `.claude/skills/`. Users place those folders themselves rather than installing them from a marketplace, so Claude Code treats them as user customization under this setting.

The four sub-key entries below list what else each surface blocks and what still loads. Claude Code ignores surface names it doesn't recognize rather than failing the settings file, so you can add new surface names before every client has updated.

### `strictPluginOnlyCustomization.skills`
### `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`

Block CLI startup until Claude Code has freshly fetched [server-managed settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md). If the fetch fails, Claude Code exits instead of continuing with cached or no settings. Set it when your environment can't accept even a brief window in which a session runs without its managed policy.

When the key is unset, Claude Code doesn't block startup on the fetch, though when the developer signs in at startup it waits up to five seconds for the fetch. [Anthropic can require the settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md#fetch-and-caching-behavior), which does block a start without them. A Cloud gateway session waits, and exits if the gateway can't be reached.

* **Scope**: [`Managed`](#scopes). Claude Code honors a `true` from any admin-controlled managed source, even one that isn't the highest-priority source.
* **Type**: Boolean
  * `true`: Claude Code blocks startup until it has freshly fetched server-managed settings, and exits if the fetch fails
  * `false`: unless Anthropic requires the settings, Claude Code doesn't block startup on the fetch, though at a sign-in startup it waits up to five seconds for the fetch
* **Default**: `false`

```json managed-settings.json theme={null}
{
  "forceRemoteSettingsRefresh": true
}
```

Set it in an MDM profile or the managed settings file to enforce fail-closed startup before the first server payload arrives. Claude Code applies the check only in sessions that fetch server-managed settings, so a session that [doesn't fetch them](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md#platform-availability) starts without waiting. The `claude auth` subcommands are exempt, so users can re-authenticate when expired credentials are why the fetch fails. See [Enforce fail-closed startup](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/server-managed-settings.md#enforce-fail-closed-startup).

### `managedSourcesBehavior`
### `deniedMcpServers`

Block specific MCP servers. Claude Code refuses to load a matching server wherever it's defined, including plugin servers, servers passed with `--mcp-config`, servers from `managed-mcp.json`, servers from [`managedMcpServers`](#managedmcpservers), and the claude.ai connectors [it fetches itself](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#how-connectors-reach-claude-code). In-process `type: "sdk"` servers are exempt; the app that started the session registers them.

* **Scope**: [`Any file`](#scopes). Entries from every file merge into one denylist, and [`allowManagedMcpServersOnly`](#allowmanagedmcpserversonly) doesn't change that. Deploy it in managed settings to enforce it.
* **Type**: array of objects, each with exactly one key: `serverName`, a string, so a claude.ai connector's display name such as `"claude.ai Slack"` works; `serverCommand`, an array of the command and its arguments matched exactly; or `serverUrl`, a URL pattern with `*` wildcards
* **Default**: unset, so no server is blocked; an empty array also blocks nothing

```json settings.json theme={null}
{
  "deniedMcpServers": [
    { "serverName": "filesystem" }
  ]
}
```

The denylist takes precedence over [`allowedMcpServers`](#allowedmcpservers), so a server on both lists is blocked. See [Policy-based control with allowlists and denylists](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/managed-mcp.md#policy-based-control-with-allowlists-and-denylists).

### `disableClaudeAiConnectors`

264:Claude Code recognizes a built-in set of Bash commands as read-only and runs them without a permission prompt in every mode, except as [`permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#permissions-blockreadsoutsideworkingdirectories) changes for paths outside your working directories. The set includes `ls`, `cat`, `echo`, `pwd`, `head`, `tail`, `grep`, `find`, `wc`, `which`, `diff`, `stat`, `du`, `cd`, and read-only forms of `git`. The set is not configurable; to require a prompt for one of these commands, add an `ask` or `deny` rule for it. In auto mode, these commands can also wait for the classifier's review; see [how the classifier evaluates actions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#how-the-classifier-evaluates-actions).
354:> Read and Edit deny rules apply to Claude's built-in file tools, to file commands Claude Code recognizes in Bash, such as `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, and `tee`, and to the targets of Bash [redirections](#redirections) such as `> file` and `< file`. They don't apply to a command that reads files without naming them, such as `grep -r pattern .` run from the directory that holds the file, or to arbitrary subprocesses that read or write files indirectly, like a Python or Node script that opens files itself. For OS-level enforcement that blocks all processes from accessing a path, [enable the sandbox](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md).
642:With neither managed settings nor a Team or Enterprise `/login` as the session's credential, the mod can approve a call that a deny rule refuses or a `PreToolUse` hook blocked. A session that runs on an API key or a long-lived [`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#generate-a-long-lived-token) instead isn't using that login, even when that login is stored.
### `allowedMcpServers`
201:| [`sandbox.network.allowLocalBinding`](#sandbox-network-allowlocalbinding) | Let [sandboxed](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md) commands listen on network ports and connect to localhost on macOS | Sandbox settings | Any file |

  **Fix:** Add these rows to the template. Raise the floor to 2.1.310, or state the gap.

  - `strictKnownMarketplaces` without `{"source":"skills-dir"}` makes skills-directory plugins under `.claude/skills/*/.claude-plugin/` stop loading (plugins/org.md L236). This is an unstated cost; plain `SKILL.md` files are unaffected.

  **Where:** `policies.ts:97-104`.

  **Fix:** Document an exception route, such as a policy config exclusion through an L3 PR.

Review vòng 2 của bước 3 không còn lỗi HIGH, còn 5 lỗi MEDIUM. Tôi đã tự kiểm lại từng điểm trên docs và sửa xong. Review vòng 3, chỉ xét phần vừa sửa, đang chạy. Bước 3 vẫn chưa commit.

**Đã sửa ở vòng 2:**
- **M1, thiếu ba pin `"$defaults"`:** phase 2 đã bỏ ba pin này của `autoMode`, trong khi chúng là khóa bảo vệ chứ không phải giá trị mặc định. Thiếu pin, một dev tự đặt `hard_deny: []` là xóa được luật built-in chống lộ dữ liệu ra ngoài (📖 auto-mode-config). Đã khôi phục và có test.
- **M2, `aws`/`pulumi`/`serverless` không hỏi ở auto mode:** các CLI này chạy ngoài sandbox, và ở auto mode chỉ classifier quyết định, không ai được hỏi. Đã thêm rule `ask` cho cả ba, để mọi mode đều hỏi (📖). README nay ghi rõ giới hạn còn lại:
  - `pulumi preview` chạy code của repo ngoài sandbox;
  - mà code đó có thể bị một lệnh trong sandbox sửa trước, không cần hỏi.
- **M3, `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` vô tác dụng:** khóa này chỉ lọc `allowRead`, và còn làm `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` không áp dụng được cho sandbox (📖). Đã bỏ.
  - README ghi rõ: sandbox chặn đọc theo danh sách deny, nên file nào trong home không có trong danh sách vẫn đọc được, rồi có thể gửi ra ngoài qua các domain được phép.
  - Thêm credential của Serverless và Pulumi passphrase.
- **M4, chi phí cho engineer:** README nay liệt kê đủ những gì sẽ lỗi trong sandbox:
  - git/gh/npm với repo hoặc registry private;
  - Docker;
  - localhost trên macOS;
  - Windows chạy native (không phải WSL2) thì Claude Code không khởi động được.

  Skill `prod-change` cũng sửa lại: engineer tự push và mở PR, vì trong sandbox agent không có credential git hay GitHub.
- **M5, wildcard dùng `?`:** IAM chấp nhận `?` (📖), nên `s3:?*` hay `*?` cũng là wildcard toàn phần. Policy đã chặn các dạng này; test giờ có 31 case.
- **Các điểm LOW:**
  - bảng lệch so với template dựng lại từ diff;
  - E10 nêu rõ những gì không được kiểm (permission set Identity Center, RDS instance, stack Serverless);
  - version floor phase 2 nâng lên 2.1.310;
  - sửa hai câu nói quá về `forceLoginMethod` và `allowedHttpHookUrls`.

**Kiểm tra:**
- Test mới bắt thêm một lỗ thật: file token Firebase chưa có trong `denyWrite`. Đã thêm.
- 12 mutation mới đều bị test bắt ✅.
- `validate.sh` rc=0: 106 test Python, 31/31 case policy, `claude plugin validate`, actionlint, zizmor, yamllint ✅.

Version floor phase 2 trong framework (vẫn ghi 2.1.285) và các giới hạn mới của layer 2 sẽ được đồng bộ ở bước 6.

**Vẫn chờ anh/chị quyết định OD21** (từ lượt trước): phase 1 có thêm deny `Read(~/.aws/**)` và `autoMode.classifyAllShell: true` không. Tôi đề xuất thêm: chi phí cho engineer gần như bằng 0, và version floor phase 1 hiện đã đủ cho cả hai.

  ### Checks that passed
  - **`ask` rules for the excluded CLIs:**
    - auto-mode-config.md: "Content-scoped ask rules … are evaluated before the classifier and always force a permission prompt, even in auto mode."
    - permission-modes.md (decision order, step 1): "Ask rules that match on a command's content … fall back to a permission prompt."

    - None with `allowManagedDomainsOnly`, which also refuses per-command domain lists in auto mode (sandboxing.md).
  - **Template diff:** I diffed phase 2 against today's `settings-hipaa.json`. Every difference appears in the deviations table or the "added" row; nothing is missing.
  - **Version floors** (settings-reference): `allowedProviders` needs 2.1.285, the `allowManagedHooksOnly` monitor block needs 2.1.310, `classifyAllShell` 2.1.193, `credentials` 2.1.221/224, `blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` 2.1.257. The README and the tests are consistent with these.
  - **Doc citations confirmed:**
    - `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` stops the read block from reaching sandboxed commands (section "Sandboxed commands under the block").
    - excludedCommands matching rules (finding 22).
    - User-scope `excludedCommands` and `allowedHttpHookUrls` merge (README-hipaa "Lists that merge across scopes").
    - `/goal` is lost under `allowManagedHooksOnly`.
    - `claude auth` is exempt from `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh`.
    - `failIfUnavailable` on native Windows, `skills-dir` behaviour, the `git log --output` example, deny rules applying to `cat`/`head`/`tail`.
    - Marketplace source fields (`sha`, `git-subdir`, `archive` `sha256`).
  - **validate.sh in a scratch copy** (actionlint, zizmor, claude 2.1.319): "Ran 106 tests … OK", "31/31 cases passed; all policies mandatory", "RESULT: all executed checks passed".

  **M1. "Every shell command through the auto-mode classifier" is overstated.**
  - Where: `examples/README.md:62` (E8 row); test name at `examples/tests/test_claude_settings.py:152` (`test_every_shell_command_classified_in_auto_mode`).
  - Evidence:
    - sandboxing.md: "Auto-allow mode works independently of your permission mode setting, with three exceptions: plan mode, an auto mode command that carries per-command allowed domains, and server-side classifier review…".
    - README-hipaa.md:113: "Sandboxed Bash commands run without a prompt while `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` is at its default of `true` … so for those commands the sandbox is the control."
    - settings-reference: `classifyAllShell` "suspends every shell allow rule". Phase 2 has only `npm test` and `npm run lint`, and README-hipaa:107 says it "changes nothing until you add managed allow rules".
  - Effect: with `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true` (OD12), most shell commands in auto mode skip the classifier, and the sandbox is the control. A grader comparing with README-hipaa will see the contradiction, and it weakens the "hygiene, not a boundary" message.
  - Fix:
    - Reword to: "shell allow rules don't skip the auto-mode classifier (`classifyAllShell`); sandboxed commands are auto-approved, so for them the sandbox is the control (OD12)".
    - Rename the test, e.g. `test_allow_rules_do_not_skip_classifier_and_defaults_pinned`.
    - The intro sentence of the E8 row mixes template features (provider lock, managed-only rules) into "Papaya's deviations". Separate "kept from the template" from "deviations".
  
  **M2. Finding 25 calls the `"$defaults"` pins "a lock"; the docs call the merge additive.**
  - Where: `examples/README.md` finding 25 (also implied in the E8 row).
  - Evidence: auto-mode-config.md: "Entries from each scope are combined. A developer can extend environment, allow, soft_deny, and hard_deny with personal entries but can't remove entries that managed settings provide. … a developer-added `allow` entry can override an organization `soft_deny` entry: the combination is additive, not a hard policy boundary."
  - Effect:
    - The pins do stop a developer from removing the built-in lists, so the `hard_deny: []` point is correct.
    - But a developer's own `autoMode.allow` or `environment` entries (in `~/.claude/settings.json`; `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` does not cover `autoMode`) can still turn `soft_deny` actions into auto-approved ones.
    - This limit is not stated anywhere (grep for `soft_deny` or "additive" in README and docs: no hits).
    - The prod impact is bounded, because the managed `ask` rules for `aws`/`pulumi`/`serverless` still prompt. Still, an overstated claim on a compliance-relevant control.
  - Fix: change "a lock" to "keeps the built-in rules in place: they can't be removed", and add one limit sentence quoting the doc: developer `allow`/`environment` entries still widen the classifier; not a policy boundary; the boundary for prod CLIs is the managed `ask` rules plus layer 1/3.

  - Where: `examples/pulumi-policy/policies.ts:40`.

    - `"*:*"`, `"s?:*"`, `"*3:*"` → no violation.
    - `" s3:*"` (leading space) → no violation.
    - `"sso-directory:Create*"` → no violation.
    - `"S3:*"`, `"IAM:Pass*"`, `"ssoadmin:*"`, `"iam:PassRol?"` → caught.
    - `"s3:???"` → caught (an over-block, harmless).

A developer can extend environment, allow, soft_deny, and hard_deny with personal entries but can't remove entries that managed settings provide. … a developer-added `allow` entry can override an organization `soft_deny` entry: the combination is additive, not a hard policy boundary."
- Effect:
  - The pins do stop a developer from removing the built-in lists, so the `hard_deny: []` point is correct.
  - But a developer's own `autoMode.allow` or `environment` entries (in `~/.claude/settings.json`; `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` does not cover `autoMode`) can still turn `soft_deny` actions into auto-approved ones.
  - This limit is not stated anywhere (grep for `soft_deny` or "additive" in README and docs: no hits).
  - The prod impact is bounded, because the managed `ask` rules for `aws`/`pulumi`/`serverless` still prompt. Still, an overstated claim on a compliance-relevant control.
- Fix: change "a lock" to "keeps the built-in rules in place: they can't be removed", and add one limit sentence quoting the doc: developer `allow`/`environment` entries still widen the classifier; not a policy boundary; the boundary for prod CLIs is the managed `ask` rules plus layer 1/3.

### LOW

**L1. Policy pack does not catch a wildcard in the service part.**
- Where: `examples/pulumi-policy/policies.ts:40`.
- Probe (compiled in a copy against @pulumi/aws 7.51.1):
  - `"*:*"`, `"s?:*"`, `"*3:*"` → no violation.
  - `" s3:*"` (leading space) → no violation.
  - `"sso-directory:Create*"` → no violation.
  - `"S3:*"`, `"IAM:Pass*"`, `"ssoadmin:*"`, `"iam:PassRol?"` → caught.
  - `"s3:???"` → caught (an over-block, harmless).
- Whether IAM accepts wildcards in the prefix is ⚠️ unverified. The IAM Action doc only describes wildcards "in the action name".
- Fix: treat any action whose service part contains `*` or `?` as a full wildcard, and trim the action string first. Optionally widen `NO_WILDCARD_SERVICES` to `sso[a-z-]*` and `identitystore[a-z-]*`, or say the prefixes are exact.

**L2. The test does not enforce the "kept as written" claim for the template.**
- Where: `examples/tests/test_claude_settings.py:242-245`, plus the `startswith` check at line 241.
- Mutation results (in a copy):
  - Removing `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` from `credentials.envVars`: tests pass (MISSED).
  - Removing `Read(~/.claude.json.backup*)`: MISSED.
  - Narrowing `Read(~/.kube/**)` to `Read(~/.kube/config)`: MISSED.
  - Adding `autoMode.allow` without `"$defaults"`: MISSED.
  - Caught: `ask` entries removed, an extra `excludedCommands` entry, `$defaults` removed, `allowManagedReadPathsOnly`, a `mask` mode on `~/.aws`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands: true`, `defaultMode` auto, `disableAutoMode`.
- Effect: "Every key of the template is kept as written except these" is a claim that no test enforces.
- Fix: commit a copy of the template (at commit `9196319`) under `schemas/` and add one test: phase 2 minus the documented deviations equals the template. Or at least assert the full template env-var and deny lists, and require an exact `Read(<path>/**)` for directories.

**L3. The reason for dropping `allowManagedReadPathsOnly` is incomplete.**
- Where: README deviations table row, and the test comment at `test_claude_settings.py:222`.
- Evidence (sandboxing.md):
  - A developer's `allowRead` entries merge ("a developer can append entries that widen the policy unless a lock covers that key").
  - A narrower `allowRead` re-opens part of a `denyRead` region ("The narrower allow re-opens that part of the denied region").
  - The lock that ignores `allowRead` under a denied path covers only repository settings.
  - Whether a `credentials.files` deny still holds against such an entry is ⚠️ unverified.
- Effect: "which phase 2 does not use" is true for managed settings only; for example a developer's `allowRead: ["~/.aws/sso"]` would be honoured. Impact is low, because the same developer can already add `excludedCommands`, which is documented.
- Fix: say that a developer's own `allowRead` can re-open parts of the deny list, an accepted limit like user `excludedCommands`. Optionally assert `"allowRead" not in sb["filesystem"]`.

**L4. "so they prompt in every mode" is slightly overstated.**
- Where: `examples/README.md:62`.
- Evidence: in `dontAsk` mode "anything that would prompt is denied" (permission-modes.md).
- Fix: "prompt (or are refused in `dontAsk`) in every mode". Bypass is disabled, so no other mode is affected.

**L5. The "extended" row of the deviations table is incomplete.**
- Where: the deviations table, row "`permissions.deny`, `sandbox.credentials`, `filesystem.denyWrite` | extended".
- Effect: the row omits `~/.serverlessrc`, `SERVERLESS_ACCESS_KEY` and `PULUMI_CONFIG_PASSPHRASE`, which are in the file and the tests, and in the E8 row ("Serverless").
- Fix: add them.

**L6. The marketplace test is stricter than the docs.**
- Where: `test_claude_settings.py:275` (`sha256` regex).
- Evidence: the marketplace reference says `sha256` is "64 hex characters, uppercase or lowercase". The test allows lowercase only.
- Effect: harmless; it only rejects a valid uppercase digest.
- Fix: optionally add `(?i)` to the regex.

### Verdict
**Not ready.** Two MEDIUM wording or claim fixes are needed (M1, M2); both are small text changes plus one test rename. The LOW items are optional, but L1 and L2 cost little and close real test gaps.
